Ten-year-old memories crash against one another inside your head — every alley looks familiar, yet not. The old locust tree at the village gate still stands, but strangers now sit on the stone bench beneath it.

en: You fumble through these fields by ten-year-old memory. The path has long been swallowed by wild grass, but the direction is still carved in your bones. Wind blows in from Fengxian county town, carrying the scent of firewood smoke.
The village head at the gate

en: The door is ajar. You push it open. The stench of mold mixed with a sickly-sweet rot hits you in the face. A dried corpse lies sprawled on the floor — thick-boned, broad-shouldered, no woman, certainly no child. You crouch down and turn over the hands; calluses on the knuckles, the marks of a hoe-handle.

en: You stand at the village entrance once more. The wind still blows from Mount Li, but now you know things have changed. The village head is dead, and the area where you once lived has transformed — they seem to have moved somewhere unfamiliar. You rarely return, and without money, over the years the village has become a foreign place.

zh: 西南角的中书省、东侧礼部衙署、右相府邸的飞檐，手指在石栏上描出轮廓。早市叫卖声断断续续，风卷起你衣角。
“雾太厚，看不清方向。”话毕，你转身望向终南山。
你点头“嗯”一声，抬手将石栏上露水抹去，目光未离城中。
你拱手：“大人见教。”身子微侧，让出半个身位。
天光未亮透，你已登乐游原东侧土坡。晨雾如纱，长安城九横九纵的坊墙从雾气中缓慢浮现，屋瓦镀上第一缕金，终南山在天边仅是一道青灰色的虚影。身后草叶沙沙响，有人踩着露水上来了，脚步声在你身后三步处停住。他没有开口，你能感到那道目光落在你的后背上。风里有早市胡饼的焦香，还有铜驼街方向传过来的隐约叫卖声。你站着，目光越过脚下的屋脊，一直看到终南山隐没在雾里。
“晨雾散了，便是另一个长安。”你对着终南山说，不看身后。
你伸手拨开挡在眼前的一枝酸枣，继续看远处，仿佛身后无人。
你微微侧身，让出半个视野，好叫那人也能看到终南山的轮廓。
秋日清晨，你沿着湿滑的石阶登上乐游原。晨雾比前几日更浓，长安城的轮廓浮在雾中，像一幅未干透的水墨画。你靠在一棵老槐树粗糙的树干上时，膝盖咯吱响了一声。远处终南山的影子在雾里时隐时现，早市的叫卖声和人语碎片断断续续随风送上来。有人登原，在你身后几步停住——拂了拂石凳上的露水，坐了下来，没说话，也没起身离开。你垂下眼，看见自己袖口的泥渍和鞋帮上干涸的草屑。
晨雾如愁，长安城在脚下摊开，屋瓦镀金，终南山隐现。有人登原，脚步声擦过你身侧，停在不远处的石栏旁。他低低说了句什么，像是自言自语，又像是对你说——风把字句吹散，只剩尾音挂在雾里。你没转头。远处早市的叫卖声断断续续，万家灯火灼眼，每一扇窗都亮得与你无关。那人站了片刻，又踏着雾气下山去了。衣角被风吹起，你抬手拢了拢，指节碰触到潮冷的石栏。
你望着渐散的人影，转身朝相反方向的草丛啐了口痰。
你掸了掸衣袖上的晨露，目光从灯火移向终南山的轮廓。
你朝那背影躬身拱手，低声说：“承蒙点拨，谢过足下。”

乐游原上薄雾如纱，长安城的轮廓在晨光中渐渐清晰。你倚着木栏，指尖在粗糙的木质上缓缓摩挲，望着远处终南山的黛青色山脊——雾气从山腰流过，像是水墨画里的留白。早市的叫卖声和炊烟一起升上来，模糊而遥远。你站在那里，风穿过衣襟，衣角轻轻拍着膝侧。身后有脚步声——一个人登上原头，在你左手边停下，也看着同一个方向。他没有说话，你也没有动。过了很久，那个人咳嗽一声，转身下山。脚步声越来越远，终南山的雾气又合拢了。
你抬头看远处飞过的一只孤鸟，没有回头。
你收回视线，继续看雾中的长安城，指尖没有离开木栏。
你侧身让出一点位置，看着那人，等他先开口。
你背靠一块半埋入土的残碑坐下，膝盖咯吱响了一声。风从原下灌上来，撩动衣摆。远处万家灯火明灭不定，像蒸腾的雾气。你听着风声，听着自己粗重的呼吸。有车马声从身后传来，停在坡下。
乐游原上，晚风萧瑟。你立于原畔，望着脚下长安城万千灯火如繁星落地。远处传来模糊的人声与笛音，夜风将它们揉碎，送到你耳中时已辨不清悲喜。你站了很久，衣袍被风灌满，身体却越来越重。不是累了，是沉了。转身下山时，有露水般凉的东西落在你手背上。
“这满城灯火，倒是替天省了蜡烛。”
伸手接住那片凉意，转身往原下走。
望灯火出神片刻，低声自语：“不知哪一盏，能为我留门。”
站在乐游原最高处。脚下万家灯火连成一片，模糊的市声被风吹散。远处断续传来笛声，不知从哪座府邸飘出。你手指在石栏上缓缓摩挲，触感冰凉粗糙。更鼓敲过一巡，声音在空旷的夜里显得格外清晰。
接过帖子看也不看，随手搁在石栏上，转身望向远处。
接过帖子，展开扫了一眼，折好收入袖中，继续看夜景。
双手接过帖子，压低声音问：“敢问主人名讳？小的好登门拜
卯时，慈恩寺钟声震荡塔檐。塔基石板湿滑，晨露反光。塔下广场上，新科进士们倚栏吟诗，佩玉相碰，有人高声念诵新题。杜甫立在塔阶旁，右手扶住第一块塔砖，指腹沿着砖面一道裂纹从左划到右。视线越过人群，锁定远处朱门与衙署的轮廓。阶上青苔在晨光中泛着暗绿。钟声歇时，他换了一只脚承重，手指仍停在裂纹尽头。
转身向塔下吟诗者，从袖中抽出一卷旧纸，迎风展开。
收回视线，在阶上蹲下，食指轻划青苔表面，起身拍手。
整了整衣襟，向最近一群进士走近两步，抱拳低首。
晨钟撞碎塔下湿雾。你登至第七层时，两腋生风。拂晓的长安城在脚下摊开如棋盘——坊市方正，街巷纵横，那些朱门与锦袍都缩成模糊的色块。塔下传来新科进士们高谈阔论的回声，被风撕成断断续续的碎片。你伸手掸了掸袖口沾着的塔灰，有几粒尘埃飘落下去，融进下界的晨光里。
你解下腰间酒葫芦，对着塔下遥遥一举，自顾饮尽。
你松了松衣领，任风吹散襟口热意，转身倚栏眺望终南山。
你侧耳听了听塔下的谈笑声，然后掸平衣褶，站直了身子。
卯时三刻，慈恩寺钟声荡开薄雾。你立在塔上第七层，手扶暗红色木栏。脚下的塔基广场上，人影渐密——青衫进士三五成群，有人展开一卷纸高声吟哦，佩玉相击声清脆。更远处，一乘朱轮车停在门外，帘子掀起半角。风从檐角穿过，吹动你袍角。你手指有一下没一下地叩着栏木，目光越过那些锦袍，落在更远处的终南山轮廓上。
对楼下吟诗声方向吐一口唾沫，转身看另一侧云雾。
收回视线，低头看自己靴尖已磨破的鞋面。
轻咳一声，整了整衣领，待下方有人抬头时微微颔首。

你沿着塔基走到北侧，在无名碑前停下。腿沉得抬不动，索性靠着石碑坐下，膝盖咯吱一声。月光被塔身切去一半，碑文的上半截泛着白，下半截埋在阴影里。你盯着几行字看了一会儿——那些名字入眼，但没入脑，像水从石面滑过。风从塔檐穿过来，铜铃响了两三声，又安静了。远处有更夫梆子响，一声长一声短，接着是几声狗叫。你坐着，脚底能感到底下砖缝的凉。坐了约莫一盏茶的时间，起了身，腿麻得厉害，扶了一把石碑才站稳。影子在地上从歪的拉成正的。你没再看碑文，顺着来路往回走。
月光被大雁塔的塔身切成两半，一半落在地面裂缝上，一半留在砖缝里的苔痕。你站在塔基边，借着微光辨认石碑上模糊的刻名——手指刚触到某一行的凹陷，头顶传来翅膀扑棱的声响。你抬头，塔铃在晃，月光里没有鸟的影子。低下头时，碑面上的月光又移动了半寸。远处墙角的阴影中有什么东西闪了一下，再看时已经暗了。
你蹲下，指尖在碑文的凹槽上划过去，像在读一封不属于自己的信。
你直起身，看着塔铃在月光里慢慢停下，然后转向远处的山影。
听到墙角声响，你侧头往暗处多看了一眼，再收回来时动作轻了些。
少陵原的晨风裹着土腥味扑面而来。远处长安城的炊烟在晨光中稀疏地升起——东边是曲江池畔的朱门烟囱，西边是贫民窟的冷灶。你站在原上，看着风把老农翻出的干土吹散，又看着远方那些豪宅在晨曦中熠熠生辉。脚跟下的土路干裂，每一步都带起一片扬尘。
衣袖被风灌满，你冲着长安方向吐出一口带土的唾沫。
蹲下身，捡起一块干裂的土坷垃，在手里捏碎。
弯腰，把被风吹歪的衣襟整了整，继续盯着远方。
少陵原上，晨风裹着雨腥扑面，衣袍灌满冷气。远处长安城楼隐在昏光里，万家屋顶无声。脚下干裂的土纹被风抹平，几只鸟低叫掠过。站得久了，眼睛盯着城里某处烟柱，肩头落下凉凉一滴。抬头看天，云已压得很低。转身时风推着背，脚步慢慢挪向坡下。
弯腰捡起一片碎瓦，对着风用力掷向远方
抬手接住一粒雨珠，看了一眼，继续望着城

少陵原的夜像一口倒扣的锅。你摸黑爬到高处，脚下碎石滚落，惊起宿鸟。远处古墓间幽绿鬼火明灭，像是地底的眼睛。你站定回望，长安城在夜色中分成明暗两半——南边灯火连成一片，北边黑得像被墨泼过。风穿过枯枝，呜呜作响，像有人在哭。你攥紧手，指节叩进掌心。

将诗稿放回案上，端起残酒饮尽，起身离席。
应声坐下，研墨展卷，俯首逐字抄录。笔尖沙沙作响。
躬身赔笑，问主人可需再加个序。随即铺纸研磨，笔不停挥。
「候着吧。」你刚转身，一位锦袍青年走近，门子立刻起身让路，堆笑拱手：「李公子来了，里头请，老爷正念叨您呢。」偏廊无桌，只有条冷板凳，檐角水滴落在青砖上，廊尽头的笑声隐约可闻。

退到偏廊坐下，将湿了的袖口拧干，垂首等待。
赔笑凑近门子，低声道「大人辛苦，小的有劳通传。」
你登上乐游原东南角那座废弃的戍楼。风从终南山方向吹来，带着黄土与野草的气味。你正望着城南一片新绿的麦田，忽然听见身后石阶上传来脚步声——先是一个穿着青色圆领袍的随从快步上来，朝你打量了一眼，走回石阶方向，朝下面喊了一句:“张郎，这里有人。”片刻后，一个头戴银冠的年轻官员登上城楼，身后跟着三五个仆役抬着食盒和席子。随从走到你面前，语气平淡:“这位先生，我家公子要在这一带摆席，烦劳先生移步。”

杜甫点头，收起袖中文稿，退至城墙东侧转角，将主位让出。
杜甫躬身致歉，一面退至墙角，一面替随从按住被风吹起的席角。

将抄笔搁回笔架，转身步出值房，不看任何人一眼。
略顿首，将公文归位，低声道“告退”，自行离去。

「来人，换一壶来。」语未毕，已转身与邻座谈及今科进士的赋作。你手中的酒杯举在半空，杯底那一层薄酒映着烛光，像一枚铜钱大小。
你放下空杯，起身走向窗边，负手看檐下竹影，再不回头。
你自斟残酒仰尽，将杯倒扣案上，对主人微微颔首。
你端起空壶，陪笑趋前：“大人兴高，待小的替大人斟满。”

你将纸条抽出，看也不看，递还给门子。“不必了。”
你折叠纸条，收好诗稿，朝门房方向拱了拱手。
你收好纸条，低声对门子说：“敢问……方才厅上哪位宾客？”
“那位客官说读过您的诗，这壶是他多要的。”酒壶搁在桌角，人已不见踪影。杜甫的视线落在壶沿未干的酒渍上，停了片刻。

接过饼，低首道声谢，咬了一口，目光落在街石上。

躬身道谢，双手捧起铜钱，连声说“谢大人赏”。
暮色中与旧友登乐游原归来，经坊间面摊。友要两碗热汤面，食毕起身，将一串铜钱搁在自家碗边，只付一碗。摊主目光随友人手中余钱移开。杜甫面前那碗面汤已凉，油花凝在碗沿，无人催促，亦无人说话。

西市胡商刘三娘的布庄新开张，请杜甫写了三副对联和四封家书。午后结账时，她从钱袋里摸出三文钱搁在算盘旁的木台上。“活计不错，拿去买饼吃罢。”三文钱在午后的阳光里泛着暗红的铜锈，一只绿头蝇落在其中一枚上，搓了搓前足。刘三娘转身去招呼看绸缎的客人，没有等杜甫回话。

说了声多谢，用袖口拂去铜钱上的灰尘，收入怀中。
拱手道谢，说承蒙娘子照顾，以后有活还望记着小的。
“有劳杜先生。”银色在烛火下暗淡，不抵文墨之费。座中宾客谈笑如常，无人注目此银。

拱手称谢，将碎银收入囊中。

你站起身，朝门外走去，檐角日影未移半步，头也不回。
你拱手还礼，端起凉茶饮尽，将名帖留在桌上，缓步离去。
你追上两步，躬身作揖：“郑兄提携则个，弟但求一饭之地。”
「那篇《华岳赋》写得真好，我叔父是考官，都说此人前程不可量——听说姓郑，是郑虔的侄子。」另一人接口：「是郑生啊，早年在城南同窗时，总见他在抄诗稿，比我还笨拙些，如今倒中了。」众人举杯，大笑。
放下酒钱，转身走入长安的夜色，不问姓名
低头苦笑，举碗向邻桌遥遥虚敬，又自顾斟满饮尽
俯身向邻桌微笑拱手，道「郑兄文章，学生曾读过几篇，着实佩服」
“郎君要见，先写一首茶诗。”案上备好纸笔，墨已研就。主人泰兴在帘后与人弈棋，棋子落声清脆。门子补一句：“老爷说了，诗写得好，这杯茶就算请你。不好——茶钱照付，人也请回。”
你站着未动，看了一眼茶碗，转身便走。
你默然坐下，提笔写一首五绝，搁笔而去。
“献丑了。”——你写了两首，问门子可需另为一首。
“听说你是诗人？我正要去户部王郎中府上拜谒，他好风雅。你替我写一首夸他清正的，这桌酒钱我结，再送你一包西域香料。”说话间将荷包往桌上一搁，眼神落向窗外，不看来人。

从怀中取出笔墨，略思后写诗四句，双手奉上

西市东街第三间纸铺，摊上堆着宣州楮纸和蜀郡麻纸。老板是个四十来岁的瘦削汉子，正用湿布擦柜台。见你路过，他抬头打量了你两眼，放下抹布，从架子上抽出一刀纸，搁在柜面上。“听说你会作诗？”他说得很随意，像在问菜价。“替我写一首夸我铺子的——笔在这，墨在这，写好了，这刀纸你拿去，不用给钱。”他说话时眼睛看着纸，没看你。
目光越过纸和老板的脸，转身迈入人流。
怔了半瞬，提笔蘸墨，低头写了几行。
躬身拱手：“愿效劳——若嫌不足，还能再添三首。”
“子美兄，我家老爷子过寿，你帮写首祝寿诗吧——不用太认真，热闹喜庆就行。”他笑着松手，从袖中取出一张宣纸和一支笔，搁在你面前的桌角上。周围的谈笑声微微停顿了一瞬，又继续起来——有人瞥了一眼你身上的旧袍，转头继续敬酒。
你未看那人，也未碰桌上纸笔，起身离席。
你微点头，拿起笔，恭书祝寿绝句，双手奉上。
你连忙起身作揖：“求之不得，能为府上效劳是小人的荣幸。”
杜登上城西乐游原，见一布衣人踞石栏最佳处，身前摆字画数轴。那人见杜走近，未及对视，迅速俯身收卷字画，手法急促，轴端磕在石栏上发出闷响。他抬眼瞥杜一眼，眼神警惕。风从终南山吹过来，吹得松散的画纸哗哗作响。那人不再看杜，只是低头用绳捆紧画轴。杜站在三步外，两人之间只有风声。
掉头走开，不看那人的字画，也不看那人。
苦笑一下，退到旁边垛口，背风而立。
上前拱手：“兄台莫怕，某只是来吹风的。”语气卑微。
东市午后，人声鼎沸。杜甫蹲在布庄檐下系松脱的麻鞋，半包干粮搁在脚边青石上。起身时，余光瞥见一个褴褛身影弯腰掠过——那包粗麦饼已不见。巷口阴影里，乞丐正背身往嘴里塞饼，咀嚼声又急又碎。杜甫系好鞋带，站直，拍了拍膝上尘土。乞丐侧头看了一眼，立刻转回去，肩膀微微塌下。人群依旧涌动，卖炭的吆喝声盖过一切。
你系好鞋带，目不斜视，转身没入人流。
你苦笑一声，紧了紧空瘪的干粮袋，迈步离开。
你走到巷口，低声道：“那位兄台，明日此时，小的还来此处。”
你撑了很久。咳嗽、头痛、发冷——你都忍了。但今天早上你连坐都坐不起来了。铜盆里的水映出一张灰败的脸。你终于承认：这次是真的病了。
你已经很久没有笑过了。久到记不清上次开怀是什么时候。胸口像压着一块石头，每个呼吸都沉甸甸的。朋友们说你想开些，可他们不知道——你连「想开」的力气都没有了。
独自扛着，对外只说不碍事

风雪已追了你三日。第一天你还能攥紧缰绳——第二天缰绳从你手里滑脱了三次——今天你连马鞭都握不住了。

你低头看自己的手：十根手指肿得像十根红萝卜，指节处的皮肤绷得发亮，隐隐透着紫黑色。你试着弯曲食指——咔。不是关节的响声，是皮肉里冰碴碎裂的声音。指尖已经完全没了知觉，像十颗不属于你的石头挂在手掌上。

这不是普通的冻疮。这冻到骨头里去了。

第七天了。你醒来的时候发现右手食指的指甲盖整个翻了起来——不是磕碰的，是冻死的。指甲底下的肉变成了黑色。不是紫黑，是焦黑，像烧过的木柴那种黑。你碰了碰，不疼。不疼才可怕。

你把手指举到眼前。指尖那截已经分辨不出原来的肤色，皮肉像腊肉一样硬，关节完全锁死。你知道那根手指已经死了。它挂在你的手上，但已经不是你的了。再过几天——也许是明天——它会从指节上脱落，留下一截白森森的骨头。这就是冻疮走到尽头的样子。

你看着自己的手。十根手指。还剩九根是活的。
午后你正在窗前翻书，忽然一股热浪从胸口涌起，双颊烧得发烫。你拿手背贴了贴脸——烫得吓人，掌心却凉得像冰块。窗外的日光暖融融的，你却觉得那光刺得人头晕。
晨起梳洗时，铜帕上赫然一摊血色。你怔怔地看着那片殷红，手指不自觉地攥紧了巾帕。\n\n秋风在窗外打着旋儿，你的命难道也要像这落叶一样了么？
夜半时分你猛地惊醒，后背湿漉漉的，亵衣粘在皮肤上黏腻不堪。月光透过窗纸洒进来，照见你枯瘦的手臂。你摸了摸额头——一手的冷汗。
你路过铜镜时瞥了一眼，愣住了。镜中那人颧骨高耸，眼窝深陷，衣袍空荡荡地挂在身上。你记得自己曾经不是这样的——曾经的面如冠玉呢？曾经的意气风发呢？
镜前呆立良久，黯然离去
你挣扎了几次都没能从榻上坐起来。四肢像灌了铅，额头烫得能煎蛋。门外有人叩门——是昨日约好同游的友人。你张了张嘴，声音哑得像破锣。
让友人进来，强撑着说说话
托人传话：今日抱恙，改日再约
一阵寒风透过窗棂钻进被衾，你蜷缩成一团，牙齿磕得咯咯响。炭盆里的火苗明明灭灭，暖不了你半分。连骨缝里都在往外冒着凉气。
一阵剧烈的咳嗽把你从案牍前拉起来。你弯腰扶住桌角，半天缓不过气。窗纸被吹得啪啪响，你的手抖得握不住笔。
长安的秋风裹着一层潮气钻进衣领。你缩了缩脖子，喉咙里泛起一阵腥甜。\n\n第二天醒来，头重如裹，四肢百骸像被人拆开又胡乱拼了回去。铜盆里的水映出一张泛着不正常潮红的脸——这大概就是「病」了。
额角像有人拿凿子在一下一下地敲。睁开眼，日光刺得你立刻又闭上。半边脸都是木的，连咀嚼都成了一种折磨。
桌上摆着你平日最爱吃的几碟小菜——莼菜羹、鲈鱼脍、桂花糕。你夹了一筷子，在嘴里嚼了嚼——咽不下去。没有味道。什么都没有味道。你放下筷子，叹了口气。
你又落榜了。\n\n巷口的酒旗簌簌地响，你坐在榻上，手里攥着那张写满朱批的试卷，眼睛里干涩得挤不出一滴泪。窗外的喧哗声像是隔了一层水——你听得到，但什么也听不进去。
你翻了个身，又翻了个身。床板硬得像棺材板，窗外的月光亮得刺眼。更鼓敲了三更——四更——五更了。天边泛起鱼肚白时，你依然睁着眼睛。又是一夜未眠。
砚台里的墨早就干透了，笔尖的毛都炸开了。案头的诗集落了厚厚一层灰，你甚至懒得吹一吹。你知道应该写点什么——你是个诗人啊——但你盯着白纸，脑子里一片空白。什么都不想做。什么都不在乎。
你推掉了所有邀约。门外的请柬堆了一摞，你连拆都懒得拆。\n\n谁也不想见。什么也不想做。诗也不想写。

你在市集中大笑不止，指着县衙的方向高声吟诵：

「君不见——黄河之水天上来，奔流到海不复回！」

路人侧目，孩童跟着起哄。你浑然不觉，只觉得胸中有一团火在烧，烧得你必须说些什么、喊些什么。

一把抓回字画卷轴，笔和纸扫落在地，转身大步跨出当铺门槛。

转身就走，袖风扫落她掌心那枚铜钱。
从袖中摸出最后半贯铜钱，往她手里塞。
走到小杌子边坐下，铺纸、研墨、提笔。
“施主，上个月你也来过——那天是王给事中进香。今天亲王来，你又来了。”说完继续扫地。雪落在他刚扫过的青石上，又积了一层。殿门紧闭，里面传来亲王与方丈的谈笑，声音在雪里闷着，不太真切。
一脚踢翻殿前的铜香炉，转身踏雪而去。
目光扫向亲王随行的侍从，试图从某个熟面孔找到缝隙。
你把肩上的雪拍掉，往殿门边又挪了半步。
“上一个和你鞋底有一样泥的人，现在已不穿这双靴了。他拿了我一枚木筹，那天起，他的靴底再没沾过寺后泥土。”他从怀里摸出一枚拇指长的旧木筹，递到离你一尺远的地方，没有催促，只是让它悬在那里。

肩颈微微一僵。鞋尖转向床边，已迈了半步。

裹紧袄子，朝那个背影喊了一句：“达夫，下次错买双靴子。”
你低头抻了抻过长的袖口，沉默了许久，才转身进屋去生火。
你摩挲着袄子上的针脚，自言自语：“这是军中的物件……可结实了。”
天宝十三载秋，李白过下杜城。他醉了，没叩你的门。后来有人在渭水边的沙地上看见一行字——是用剑尖划出的“杜子美”三字，歪斜潦草，旁边散落着马蹄印，延伸向潼关方向。那人来告诉你时，沙上的字迹已被风吹浅了一半。

盯着字迹直到日影偏移，用袖子抹平那片沙地，字迹消失后离去。

就着菜市的喧嚷大声念出旧作，念到第三句时郑虔回头，两人隔着人潮笑了。

抄起案上的酒壶砸向那两张并置的诗笺——但酒壶在手中转了半圈，只倒了一杯，自己喝了。
从席上滑跪下去，额头抵在两种笔迹交叠的诗笺上——但膝盖锁死在袍摆里，站不起来。
欠身拿起两张诗笺端详，顺着韵脚往下比对，评了一句“第三字若用去声会更稳”，把话题转向用典。

「祭文，润笔两贯。」比市价少了八贯。他用的不是商量的语气，是提醒——去年你替他外甥润色过的那篇行状，至今没付过一字润金。
砚台推过桌心，墨汁泼上那张素笺。
问了一句：隔壁背书的那篇，可是来年应试的篇目？
把素笺在桌面铺平，提笔蘸了最后一点墨。
巡按的笑声透过屏风传过来——他们在聊长安新到的阳羡茶，语气松散得像聊自家园子的杏花。张主簿推过一摞账册，翻到第四页，笔杆点了点那个数字。“跟第七页对不上吧。”他说这话时没看你，语气像在吩咐一个知道规矩的人。你知道他为什么这么跟你说话——上次帮他整理那些说不清来源的租契时，你问过一句“总数要不要盘”，他用同样的笔杆在同样的位置点了两下。那个墨点还在。
指间的笔砸在账册上，墨迹横过四页的数字。

肩头残余的拍击温度还没散。你把门框上挂着的那壶浊酒拎下来，壶底朝上搁在门槛正中间。
你没看那年轻人，只对李十二郎问了一句：“韦侍郎最近还在收碑帖？”
你把椅子从桌前往后挪了半寸，伸手去接那卷诗稿。
门帘掀开半幅，薛家管事站在槛外没进来。他将二两碎银搁在桌上——纸包摊开，糙纸上还粘着昨夜的油渍。“明晚有个小宴，请先生来添点文气。”你到的时候发现座位在最下手，离门最近，离炉子最远。离你最近的那道菜端上来时就已经凉了。薛三郎坐在上首，跟身旁的人聊着你上次替他润色的那篇碑文——他不记得你叫什么，他叫你“上次那个人”。
将凉了的菜碟往桌心一推，起身走向门口。

脂粉味和荔枝的甜腻混在一起，把空气搅成黏稠的浆。紫袍胖子靠在锦垫上，三根手指捏着剥好的荔枝，汁水沿指缝往下走，滴在袍子上洇出深色的印。一个家丁的手不知什么时候扣住了你的肘弯，指节收紧时你听见自己袖口的布料发出绷紧的声响。胖子没转头。他用下巴朝角落指了一下——地上铺着一张毡垫，垫子上几根鸡毛粘在干涸的湿痕边缘。“杜审言的孙子？正好。”他把荔枝核吐在歌伎递来的银盘里，“我这鸡刚赢三场，缺一首压轴的。你坐那写。”歌伎中的一个用扇子掩了嘴，眼睛从你脸上扫到毡垫上那摊湿痕，扇子后面有气音漏出来。
他抽回被攥住的胳膊，转身朝门外走，脚步在门槛前停下，没有回头。
他走向毡垫，跪下时膝盖压住一根鸡毛，铺纸研墨的手没有抖。
他朝毡垫走了两步，停住，转过身看着胖子的侧脸，没有坐下的意思。

坊墙下的风是从北边灌进来的。年老的那个挡在你面前，离你三步，刚好占住你唯一能起身的方向。年轻的站在你身后，你听见他的手指一下一下拨着刀环，铁碰铁，不高不低，像在敲一种不需要旋律的拍子。年老的那个没有催，他把那个名字又说了一遍，放慢了说，像在教一个孩童认字。然后他从袖中取出一卷纸，展开——是空白的，只在上方端正地压了一方朱砂印。他将纸放在你膝边的冻土上，压了一小块碎银在纸角。风把纸边掀起一点，又落下。
杜甫起身，将膝边那张纸连带碎银一起从冻土上拨开，从两人之间走过。
杜甫伸手按住被风掀动的纸角，从怀中摸出笔，在冻土上润了润墨。
杜甫没碰那张纸，只问了一句：“碑刻成之后，拓片能带回长安一卷么？”

纸灰飞进眼睛时门被推开了。不是风吹的。那人停在门槛外，停了好一会儿——你跪在蒲团上，他站在门槛外，中间隔着昨夜烧尽的纸灰和今日尚未烧的纸钱。他不进来。庙里的寒气从地面往上漫，他站在门外仅一步远的地方，靴跟在石阶上轻轻磕了两下。“杜先生，就一句——今日午时，一首贺诗，老地方，要喜庆。”他没进来，只把话搁在门槛外，踩着你昨夜烧的纸灰转身走了。你回头时只看见他背影。靴跟上沾着黑色残烬。庙外他的马打了个响鼻，声音在空荡荡的大殿里弹了三个来回才落定。

“看见这洞了么？屋里比屋外还冷三分。”他没有进屋，只是隔着门帘吩咐：子美，出来走两步，让她们看看你是怎么过冬的。帘子那头没有回应。他笑了一声，不高不低：“不打紧，我等得起。”
他掀开破被子站起来，直直走出门，站在雪地里，不说话。
他展开纸，不等对方开口，已开始默写昨日未完成的诗句。
“大人既喜观清寒，可愿听一句实话？”他隔着门帘开口，语气平和。

他端起碗，没有喝——松手。碗碎，泔水飞溅。他推门便走。
不等对方说完，他已经走到矮几前展开那张纸，提笔蘸墨。
“大人说的举荐信，落款是哪位府君的印？”
“子美兄，我有个同僚想见户部的人。价钱好说。”说这话时他的眼睛没看你，看的是你身后那扇门——门后是今日宴席上所有正在交易的秘密。他笃定你还在这张桌上。

堆出笑容，双手捧起酒壶为对方斟满。
沉默片刻，问他那位同僚手里有什么可以交换。
“客人又来了。”他说完就走了，托盘在肘边晃了一下，映出灯影——那块漆掉了一块，露出旧木，上次你见它时还没掉。
名帖往地上一掷，转身踩着新靴踏出廊去。
腰一弯，笑容堆满脸，双手将名帖捧过头顶。
掂了掂袖中另一条消息，走向厅侧等他的管事。
东市茶肆二楼临窗的位置，一个绸缎商把一张纸条推过案面。纸上只写着一个官员的名字，墨迹已干。他将茶碗搁在纸条旁边，碗底在纸上压出一圈湿痕。“上次你在盐商老张那儿‘问’的事，我听说过。”目光越过碗沿，不紧不慢地看着你，“我不是来为难你的。我也是来做生意的。”窗外楼下，东市的骡马队正在卸货，鞭子抽在青石板上的声响传上来。绸缎商从袖口又抽出一张叠好的纸，“这是价钱。你看看。”
拂袖将茶碗扫落，纸条在湿痕里裂成两半。
双手接过那张报价单，脸上堆出笑容，腰已弯下三分。
指尖压住纸条一角，不翻也不推，只问他要的这个名字，市价几何。
铁钩刮过石板的声音先于坊丁的身影抵达。你起先以为坊墙下是一堆破被褥，走近三步才看清被褥里伸出的半只手——手指收拢，掌心空着，指甲暗紫色。坊丁走近时你往后退了一步，手不自觉伸进怀里，指腹触到那几枚铜钱，还在。铜钱贴着肋骨，温热。你停了半秒，把铜钱在指间转了一下，按回原处。坊丁弯下腰时你已从他和那具身体旁绕了过去，袖口蹭过坊墙的粗面，带下一撮干土。
袖口蹭过坊墙，干土簌簌落下。你继续穿过路口。
一道老裂痕从云纹中间贯过去，朝奉把它在窗口的光下翻了翻放回柜台。“死当？”你说是。他报的数刚好够付欠了半月的房租和三斗米。你没有还价。帕子在指间叠成方块时，原先包玉的凹处还带着一点余温，四角被玉佩压出的棱硌进掌心。麻绳从栅栏那边推过来，铜钱在绳上沉甸甸地响了一声。你松开帕子，把铜钱拨进袖口——手腕内侧那块被玉焐了十年的皮肉现在贴上了冰凉的方孔。
站住。袖口往下坠了一坠。继续往米铺走。

他在门口站定时你正数着袖里的铜钱。余光先触到那件青衫——经纬洗得松了，透出里层麻布的纹路。他往前迈了一步，门槛的阴影从他脚背移到脚踝。你听见自己的脊椎一节节凉下去。他问“先生在长安怎么才能被人看见”。你张开嘴。舌根往上颚顶了一下。然后你听见一句话从自己喉咙里出来——“好好写，总会有人看见的”。那声音薄得像坊墙外飘进来的叫卖。他低着头认真点头，袖子里摸出一截秃笔，用唾沫润了润笔尖，抬头说“您再说一遍，我记一记”。你说不用记了。他写字的姿势让你想起十年前租住在城南土墙房里，每天蘸井水在桌上练字的时辰。
顿一下。把那截秃笔推还给他。
{npc_name} 支支吾吾，半天憋不出一个字，尬住了…
{npc_name} 巧妙地吟出了「{keyword}」字，满座皆惊！
en: {npc_name} stammers and stutters, unable to squeeze out a single word... How awkward.

zh: {npc_name} 憋了半天，没能对上联句，气氛有些尴尬…
en: {npc_name} deftly chants the word "{keyword}", stunning everyone present!

zh: {npc_name} 以「{@lianju_npc_name}」为题，吟出一联，满座击节赞叹！
en: {npc_name} struggles for a long moment but fails to match the couplet. The mood turns awkward...
{npc_name} takes "{@lianju_npc_name}" as the theme and recites a couplet, drawing thunderous applause from all!

zh: 腹中隐隐作痛，这毒物怕不是那日试药留下的…

en: A dull ache lingers in your stomach — this poison must be from that day you tested the medicine...

zh: 腹中隐隐作痛，这毒物怕不是那日试药留下的…

en: A dull ache lingers in your stomach — this poison must be from that day you tested the medicine...

zh: 脚踝还在隐隐发疼，走路得慢些。

en: Your ankle still throbs faintly. Best take it slow.
In 735, a young Du Fu journeyed to Mount Tai.

zh: 745年，杜甫初入长安，怀抱功名之志

en: In 745, Du Fu first arrived in Chang'an, his heart burning with ambition for official renown.

zh: 掸了掸肩上露水，头也不回地朝雾中走去。
en: Entering the World / Pursuit of Renown

zh: 收回目光，继续看着雾中的终南山影。
en: He brushed the dew from his shoulders and walked into the mist without looking back.

zh: 稍稍侧身，给对方腾出半边靠着的树身。
en: He withdrew his gaze and continued watching the silhouette of Mount Zhongnan in the mist.

zh: 秋日清晨，你沿着湿滑的石阶登上乐游原。晨雾比前几日更浓，长安城的轮廓浮在雾中，像一幅未干透的水墨画。你靠在一棵老槐树粗糙的树干上时，膝盖咯吱响了一声。远处终南山的影子在雾里时隐时现，早市的叫卖声和人语碎片断断续续随风送上来。有人登原，在你身后几步停住——拂了拂石凳上的露水，坐了下来，没说话，也没起身离开。你垂下眼，看见自己袖口的泥渍和鞋帮上干涸的草屑。
en: He shifted slightly, making room against the tree for the other person to lean on.

An autumn morning. You climb the slippery stone steps to Leyou Plateau. The morning mist is thicker than days before — the outline of Chang'an floats in the fog like an unfinished ink-wash painting. As you lean against the rough bark of an old locust tree, your knee creaks. In the distance, Mount Zhongnan's shadow flickers in and out of the mist. Fragments of hawking cries and human chatter drift up intermittently on the wind. Someone else ascends the plateau, stopping a few paces behind you — brushes dew from a stone bench, sits down, says nothing, and does not rise to leave. You lower your eyes and notice the mud stains on your cuffs and the dried blades of grass clinging to your shoes.

zh: 你站起身，对着那片灯火长长吐出一口浊气。
你抽出腰间酒囊，仰头灌了一口，又将目光投向远处。
en: You rise to your feet and let out a long, heavy breath toward the sea of lantern lights.

zh: 你侧耳细听那车马声，辨认来人身份，手按膝头缓缓站起。
en: You pull the wine flask from your belt, tilt your head back for a swig, then cast your gaze toward the distance.

zh: 你背靠一块半埋入土的残碑坐下，膝盖咯吱响了一声。风从原下灌上来，撩动衣摆。远处万家灯火明灭不定，像蒸腾的雾气。你听着风声，听着自己粗重的呼吸。有车马声从身后传来，停在坡下。
en: You strain your ears at the sound of cart and horse, trying to discern the visitor's identity, then press a hand to your knee and slowly stand.

You sit with your back against a half-buried broken stele, your knee letting out a creak. The wind surges up from below the plateau, tugging at your robes. In the distance, ten thousand lantern lights flicker like steaming mist. You listen to the wind and to your own labored breath. The sound of cart and horse comes from behind, stopping at the foot of the slope.

zh: 对着无名碑哼了一句乡谣，转身去拨弄塔铃。
en: Leaning Against Stone, Listening to Lanterns

zh: 收下这片月光，拍了拍膝上的灰，望向远处。
en: He hummed a line of a hometown tune to the nameless stele, then turned to toy with the pagoda bells.

zh: 倚着碑时调整了腰背的弧度，让脊骨贴合石面的凉意。
en: He gathered this patch of moonlight, dusted off his knees, and gazed into the distance.

zh: 你沿着塔基走到北侧，在无名碑前停下。腿沉得抬不动，索性靠着石碑坐下，膝盖咯吱一声。月光被塔身切去一半，碑文的上半截泛着白，下半截埋在阴影里。你盯着几行字看了一会儿——那些名字入眼，但没入脑，像水从石面滑过。风从塔檐穿过来，铜铃响了两三声，又安静了。远处有更夫梆子响，一声长一声短，接着是几声狗叫。你坐着，脚底能感到底下砖缝的凉。坐了约莫一盏茶的时间，起了身，腿麻得厉害，扶了一把石碑才站稳。影子在地上从歪的拉成正的。你没再看碑文，顺着来路往回走。
en: Leaning against the stele, he adjusted the arch of his back, letting the stone's coolness press against his spine.

You walk along the pagoda's base to the north side and stop before a nameless stele. Your legs are too heavy to lift, so you simply sit against it — your knee creaks. The pagoda body cuts the moonlight in half: the upper half of the inscription gleams pale white, the lower half buried in shadow. You stare at a few lines — the names enter your eyes but not your mind, like water gliding over stone. Wind threads through the pagoda eaves; the bronze bells chime two or three times, then fall silent. In the distance, a night watchman's clapper sounds, one beat long, one beat short, followed by a few barks of a dog. You sit, the soles of your feet sensing the chill of the brick seams beneath. After roughly the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, you rise — your legs have gone numb; you steady yourself against the stele before standing firm. Your shadow on the ground stretches from crooked to straight. You do not look at the inscription again, and retrace your steps the way you came.

zh: 站起来拍拍土，转身朝鬼火方向走去。
en: Withered Vigil Before the Stele — Moon Sets, Wind Stills

zh: 从腰间解下水囊，仰头灌了一口，继续盯着远处的长安。
en: He rose, dusted himself off, and turned to walk toward the will-o'-wisps.

zh: 解下外袍折好垫在石头上，调整姿势靠得更舒服些。
en: He unclasped the waterskin from his belt, tilted his head back for a drink, and kept staring at distant Chang'an.

zh: 深夜少陵原，鬼火在古墓间游移。你在枯树下靠了许久，腿酸了，背疼了，索性坐下。风穿过枯枝呜呜作响，远处长安城的灯火明明灭灭。你数了几遍，数到一半忘了数到哪，干脆不数了。膝盖咯吱响了一声，你揉了揉，没动。
en: He removed his outer robe, folded it neatly as a cushion on the stone, and adjusted his posture to lean more comfortably.

Deep night on Shaoling Plain — will-o'-wisps drift among ancient tombs. You've been leaning against a withered tree for so long your legs ache and your back hurts, so you simply sit. Wind moans through the dead branches; the lights of Chang'an flicker in the distance. You tried counting them several times, but midway through you'd forget where you were — so you stopped counting altogether. Your knee creaks. You rub it, but do not move.

zh: 747年，杜甫经历了官场失意后逐渐走向旷达

en: In 747, after suffering official setbacks, Du Fu gradually moved toward a more uninhibited, expansive outlook.

zh: 放下酒杯，侧耳继续听下去。
邻桌几个汉子正说得热闹，唾沫星子飞溅。其中一个拍着桌子：「我家那小子烧了三天三夜，城南那几家药铺都走遍了，银子花了一箩筐，屁用没有！后来经人指点找了西市那位神医——就三剂药，隔天就能下地跑！」旁边的人纷纷凑头过去打听住处。你端起酒杯抿了一口，记下了这个名字。
en: You set down your cup and tilt your ear to keep listening.

A few men at the next table are in the thick of animated talk, spittle flying. One slams the table: "My boy burned with fever for three days and nights — we tried every apothecary in the south of the city, spent a basketful of silver, completely useless! Then someone pointed us to that divine physician in the West Market — three doses of medicine, and the next day he was up and running!" The men around him lean in eagerly, asking for the address. You raise your cup for a sip and tuck the name away in memory.

zh: 怎么办....你跌跌撞撞的跑了出去
你恍惚了一下，想起了昨天的遭遇。几乎是绝望的，你的脸一下子煞白，瘫坐在地上。手指用力抓住地面，探索着你中道崩卒的理想路径。
en: What now... You stumble out in a daze.

Your mind goes blank for a moment as yesterday's ordeal floods back. Nearly despairing, your face turns ashen and you slump to the ground. Your fingers claw at the earth, groping for the path your ideals took when they died halfway.

zh: 一路上，你都在愤恨着。你知道自己的才华，但这个杀千刀的世界，右相大人，就没来由的拦截了你。

en: All along the way, you seethe with indignation. You know your own talent — but this godforsaken world, His Excellency the Chancellor, has blocked you for no reason at all.

zh: “既然庙堂朽坏，我便去结交这世间真正的风流人物！太白兄、摩诘兄（王维），只要与他们诗酒唱和，让我李杜之名响彻长安，何愁大唐没有我施展抱负的青天！”
你坐在角落里喝着闷酒。隔壁桌的几个太学生正在高声谈论：“听说了吗？太白先生昨日在沉香亭，醉草吓蛮书，连高力士都得给他脱靴！只凭这惊世的诗才，皇上便赐了他翰林供奉！”你握着酒杯的手微微一颤。你的脑海中闪过李林甫那张阴沉的脸，又闪过李白狂放的笑声。一条隐秘而辉煌的道路，在你面前徐徐展开。
en: "Since the court is rotten, I shall seek out the truly remarkable souls of this age! Brother Taibai, Brother Mojie (Wang Wei) — if I can trade poems and wine with them and make the name Li-Du resound through Chang'an, then surely the Tang dynasty will offer a sky broad enough for my ambitions!"

You sit in the corner nursing a bitter cup of wine. At the next table, several Imperial Academy students are talking loudly: "Have you heard? Yesterday at the Aloeswood Pavilion, Master Taibai drafted a letter to intimidate the barbarians while drunk — even Gao Lishi had to pull off his boots for him! For his world-shaking poetic genius alone, the Emperor appointed him Hanlin Academician!" Your hand trembles slightly around the wine cup. Before your mind's eye flash two images: Li Linfu's grim face, and then Li Bai's wild, unrestrained laughter. A hidden but glorious path slowly unfolds before you.

zh: ...睁开眼睛，先于阳光袭来的是一股酒精的味道和一股恶臭。你下意识准备爬起来，但手摸到的不是自家床榻通常的柔软被子，而是坚硬的石头。稍微直起身来。你看见一个颓废的老头，胡须花白，正睡在你对面。矮桌上还有半盏没喝完的酒。你一阵眩晕想吐。强撑着站起来，扶着墙，真准备往右相府门口走。

en: ...You open your eyes. Before the sunlight hits, the stench of stale alcohol and something foul assaults you first. You instinctively try to get up, but your hand finds not the soft bedding of your own bed, but hard stone. You prop yourself up slightly. You see a disheveled old man with a graying beard, asleep across from you. On the low table between you, half a cup of unfinished wine. A wave of dizziness and nausea washes over you. You force yourself to stand, brace against the wall, and prepare to head toward the Chancellor's gate.

zh: 尽管失败于一手遮天的右相府，你仍然相信你可以通过各种方法获得官职，清整这个世界。

en: Though defeated by the all-powerful Chancellor's office, you still believe you can obtain an official post through other means and set this world right.

zh: 你变成了狂客。是真狂还是假旷达，真逃避？谁也说不清。
你不止一次想起来自己的老婆孩子——但更多的是自己的政治报复。你曲意逢迎，希望这样可以带来好结局。
en: You have become a Mad Poet. Is it real madness, or false detachment — true escape? No one can say.

zh: 你被生活的重压折弯了腰，你不再在意什么政治，你唯一关系的就是填饱自己的肚子。
en: More than once you've thought of your wife and children — but even more of your political vengeance. You bend and fawn, hoping it will bring a good outcome.

zh: 你的城府与心计。城府越高，势衰减越小，浊流交互消耗大减，但你的声望积累会因此放缓。
en: The crushing weight of life has bent your back. You no longer care about politics — your only concern is filling your belly.
Your depth of guile and cunning. The higher your astuteness, the slower your Momentum decays and the less corruption drains you — but your Prestige accumulation will slow as a result.
Your guile deepens by the day.
You plot from the shadows, revealing nothing.
You overturn clouds and rain — one hand blots out the sky.
All defenses shattered — nothing left to hide behind.

zh: 如果你回不去，你的尸体和路边那些无名的流民混在一起，被同一场大雪掩埋。远在奉先的妻子还在等一个永远不会到来的好消息。你甚至没能看一眼那个被大火点燃的乱世
你终于拿到了那身发绿的从八品下官服。你迫不及待地想要向奉先县的妻儿报喜。这十年的长安风雪，终究是没有白挨。只要穿过骊山，渡过那条结冰的河，一切都会好起来的。大概吧。
en: If you don't make it back, your corpse will mingle with those nameless refugees by the roadside, buried by the same blizzard. Far away in Fengxian, your wife is still waiting for good news that will never come. You won't even get to witness the world set ablaze by the coming chaos.

You've finally received that greenish Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade official robe. You can't wait to bring the good news to your wife and children in Fengxian County. These ten years of Chang'an's wind and snow — they were not in vain after all. Just cross Mount Li, ford that frozen river, and everything will be fine. Probably.

zh: 冷。官服的布料比你想象的还要单薄。腰带在寒风中断裂，僵硬的手指甚至无法将它重新打结。没关系，只要走快一点，风就追不上你
风里飘来极其浓郁的肉香和温泉的暖意。那是骊山，是你这十年苦苦拜谒的权贵们冬日寻欢的地方。路边的雪堆里倒着几个僵硬的流民，你低着头，不敢看他们，也不敢看骊山。
en: Cold. The fabric of the official robe is thinner than you imagined. The belt snaps in the freezing wind — your stiff fingers cannot even tie it back together. No matter. Walk faster, and the wind won't catch you.

zh: 猛风把天地撕成碎片。你失去了方向，只剩下一具凭本能在雪地里挪动的躯壳。你开始怀疑，从八品下的俸禄，真的能买到足够全家人过冬的生麦吗？
en: The wind carries the rich aroma of roasting meat and the warmth of hot springs. That is Mount Li — where the powerful you've spent ten years groveling before go to seek winter pleasures. In the snowdrifts by the roadside lie several frozen refugees. You lower your head, not daring to look at them — nor at Mount Li.

zh: 你到了。那个漏风的茅草屋就在前面。推开门，你就能看见他们了。
en: The fierce wind tears heaven and earth to shreds. You've lost your bearings — nothing remains but a husk crawling through the snow on sheer instinct. You begin to wonder: can the salary of a Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade official truly buy enough raw wheat to last the whole family through winter?
You've arrived. That drafty thatched hut is right ahead. Push open the door, and you'll see them.
Take off the official robe and put on the tattered padded jacket.

zh: 你引以为傲的、朝廷刚发的那身从八品下绿色官服，用的是最劣质的单薄丝帛，在雪地里吸满水后结成了冰甲。
en: Wrap the official robe tighter and tough it out.

The green Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade official robe — the one you were so proud of, freshly issued by the court — is made of the cheapest, thinnest silk. Soaked through in the snow, it has frozen into a suit of ice.

zh: 门开了。屋里比外面更冷。没有哭声。土炕上的那个小小的襁褓，已经和底下的稻草[glitch level=5.0]冻结成了一块坚硬的冰疙瘩[/glitch]。你本能地想要把怀里那层象征身份的绿袍脱下来盖上去，但那层布料早就被风雪撕成了碎条。大唐的从八品下右卫率府兵曹参军，站在大唐的盛世里。你试图调用那个名为‘父亲’的接口，但物理世界只向你抛回了[glitch level=10.0]ERR_TARGET_ENTITY_DEAD[/glitch]。

en: The door opens. Inside is colder than outside. No crying. On the earthen bed, that tiny swaddled bundle has, along with the straw beneath it, [glitch level=5.0]frozen into a solid block of ice[/glitch]. Instinctively, you reach to take off that green robe — the emblem of your status — and cover it over, but the fabric was long ago torn to shreds by wind and snow. The Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade Right Guard Commandery Staff Officer of the Great Tang stands in the glorious heyday of the empire. You attempt to invoke the interface named "Father," but the physical world only throws back [glitch level=10.0]ERR_TARGET_ENTITY_DEAD[/glitch].

zh: 你摸着身上那层发绿的从八品下官服。你突然意识到一个极其恐怖的逻辑悖论……

en: You touch the greenish Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade official robe on your body. A terrifying logical paradox suddenly dawns on you...
[Silently I ponder the jobless wanderers, then think of soldiers guarding distant frontiers.]

zh: 死死盯住这墙外的冻死骨
en: Close your eyes and hurry past.

zh: 骊山的行宫里，天子正在论功行赏。那是大唐的最高 API 接口，输出着绝对的恩典与仁慈。但你低头看着路边那具衣不蔽体的女尸，你的大脑陷入了死循环。你从小学习的《论语》告诉你，雷霆雨露皆是君恩；但十年长安的常识告诉你，骊山里赏赐的每一匹丝绸，都精准对应着墙外某个被抽干鲜血的家庭。国家没有缺陷，天子依然圣明，只是大唐的注意力不再分配给这些路边的冻死骨了。
en: Stare hard at the frozen corpses outside the walls.

In the mountain palace on Mount Li, the Son of Heaven is distributing rewards. That is the Tang dynasty's highest API interface, outputting absolute grace and benevolence. But you look down at the half-naked female corpse by the roadside, and your brain enters an infinite loop. The Analects you studied since childhood tells you that both thunder and rain are the Emperor's grace; yet ten years of common sense in Chang'an tells you that every bolt of silk rewarded inside Mount Li corresponds precisely to some family outside these walls that has been drained of its blood. The state has no flaws. The Son of Heaven remains sagely. It's just that the Tang dynasty no longer allocates attention to these frozen corpses by the roadside.

zh: 盯着灞桥，直到雪盖满身
灞桥的残柳被冻成铁丝。你努力挺直腰板，试图让那身薄得透风的从八品下绿袍显出几分官威，好对得起这十年的卑躬屈膝。你本想饮尽最后一口浊酒赋诗一首，但冻僵的酒壶粘住了嘴唇，撕下一层皮。狂风灌进胃里，把你精心排练的衣锦还乡，吹成了一个毫无知觉的死循环。
en: Stare at Ba Bridge until the snow covers you completely.

The withered willows of Ba Bridge have frozen into iron wire. You strain to straighten your back, trying to make that paper-thin Junior Eighth-Rank green robe project some official dignity — to justify these ten years of groveling. You meant to drain the last mouthful of cheap wine and compose a poem, but the frozen flask sticks to your lips and tears off a layer of skin. The gale pours into your stomach, and the triumphant homecoming you so carefully rehearsed is blown into a senseless, endless loop.

zh: 那扇漏风的破木门就在眼前。门缝里透不出半点柴火的光。你僵硬的手指正要触碰门环，一阵极其沉闷的啼哭声穿透了木板。这声音不像是属于人间的，它像是在你冻僵的颅骨腔内直接震荡。
[shake rate=15 level=4]（开门... 开门... 我是从八品下的官员... 我带了俸禄回来... 只要开门一切都会好起来的...）[/shake]
en: That drafty, broken wooden door is right before you. Not a sliver of firelight seeps through the cracks. Your stiff fingers are about to touch the door ring when an exceedingly muffled wail pierces through the wood. This sound does not seem to belong to the mortal world — it resonates directly inside your frozen skull.
[shake rate=15 level=4](Open the door... open the door... I am a Junior Eighth-Rank official... I've brought back my salary... just open the door and everything will be fine...)[/shake]

zh: 你感觉逐渐和豪强们打好关系了，现在应该开始实际请求他们的支持了
en: I will pass the exam! Rise up, man of Tang!
You feel you've gradually built rapport with the powerful families. It's time to start asking for their actual support.

zh: 你的行卷辗转递到了{@npc_name}手中。这位大人翻阅了片刻，虽未当场表态，却也没有随手丢弃——而是将你的诗文收进了案头的卷宗里。你瞧在眼中，心中燃起一线希望。

en: Your scroll of writings eventually makes its way into the hands of {@npc_name}. The esteemed personage leafs through it for a moment. Though no commitment is made on the spot, neither is your work casually discarded — instead, your poems are tucked into the dossier on the desk. You catch this from the corner of your eye, and a thread of hope kindles in your heart.

zh: 你递上名帖候见，门人延请入内。{@npc_name}倒也和气，虽未予你什么明确的承诺，却也让座奉了茶，问了几句近来的文章。出门时你细细回味，觉得这一趟不算白来。
en: Like Clay Oxen Into the Sea

You present your name card and wait for an audience. The attendant invites you inside. {@npc_name} is cordial enough — while no explicit promise is made, you are offered a seat and tea, and asked a few questions about your recent writings. As you leave, you reflect carefully: this trip was not in vain.

zh: 递上新诗，主家展卷细读，缓缓点头。虽说今日并未许下任何承诺，但那扇门至少没有当面关上。

en: You present your new poem. The host unrolls it, reads carefully, and slowly nods. Though no promises were made today, at least the door was not shut in your face.

zh: 拱手称谢，心中暗记此人的名号。
你在西市巷陌间辗转打听，终于寻到了那间不起眼的医庐。门帘半卷，药香扑鼻。神医正在院里翻晒药材，见你来访也不惊讶，只指了指檐下的竹凳让你坐。你递上名帖，他放下手中的药杵，用粗布擦了擦手，接过去看了看。「你就是他们说的那个杜甫？」他笑着斟了一碗药茶推过来，「我听过你的诗。坐，不急。」
en: You cup your hands in thanks, silently memorizing the name.

After asking around the alleys of the West Market, you finally locate that unassuming medical hut. The door curtain is half-drawn; the scent of medicine fills the air. The divine physician is in the courtyard, turning over drying herbs. He is not surprised by your visit — merely points to a bamboo stool under the eaves and gestures for you to sit. You hand him your name card. He sets down his pestle, wipes his hands on a coarse cloth, and takes it for a look. "So you're the Du Fu they speak of?" He smiles, pours a bowl of herbal tea, and slides it toward you. "I've heard your poems. Sit. No rush."

zh: 那封密信被原封不动地退了回来。当晚，一群黑衣家丁堵住了你的归路。拳脚如雨，你在泥地里蜷作一团，肋骨传来清脆的断裂声。把柄已然暴露——但对方翻脸不认账。

en: The secret letter is returned, unopened. That very night, a group of black-clad household guards block your way home. Fists and kicks rain down; you curl into a ball in the mud as a crisp crack rings from your ribs. The leverage has been exposed — but the other side simply denies everything.

zh: 一封密信递入门房，对方的脸色从倨傲变成惶惑。三日后，银两如数送至。那扇朱门，如今见你远远绕道而行。

en: A secret letter is delivered to the gatehouse. The recipient's expression shifts from arrogance to alarm. Three days later, the silver is delivered in full. That vermilion gate — now they take a wide detour at the sight of you.

zh: 朱门紧闭，闻说主人病重，谢绝一切宾客
en: Present your name card and await audience — knock at the vermilion gates.
The vermilion gates are shut tight. Word is the master is gravely ill — all visitors are turned away.

zh: 诗尚可,把名字抹了,改日送与刘参军.又转头向你笑道:赐坐,赏你一壶茶.侍从端来一壶冷茶

en: "The poem is passable. Erase the name and send it to Adjutant Liu another day." He turns to you with a smile: "A seat for you, and grant him a pot of tea." The attendant brings a pot of cold tea.

zh: 试图用袖口擦去上面的泥水...
en: Cold Tea and a Cast-Off Draft

zh: 越擦越黑。【致君尧舜上，再使风俗淳】的墨迹彻底化开了。
en: You try to wipe the mud off with your sleeve...

zh: 人群终于散去。那卷轴已经和泥水糊成了一团黑泥，散发着腥臭。
en: The more you rub, the blacker it gets. The ink of "[Serve the Emperor as Yao and Shun were served, and restore purity to the customs of the age]" has smeared beyond recognition.

zh: 你看着他，又看了看自己脚下那摊糊满泥水的干谒诗稿...
en: The crowd finally disperses. The scroll has congealed with mud and water into a lump of black sludge, reeking of filth.

zh: 你呆立在泥水坑前。不远处的酒肆屋檐下，你看到了国子监广文馆博士郑虔。他正把几枚生锈的铜钱排在案上，换了一角最劣质的浊酒。一阵风吹过，你曾以为他那身打满补丁却洗得发白的青衫是名士的‘清流作秀’，直到此刻，你看到他在寒风中不受控制地瑟缩了一下，却依然小心翼翼地用袖口护着怀里那方廉价的残墨。
en: You look at him, then down at the pile of mud-caked patronage poems at your feet...

zh: 犹豫了一下，你勉强的笑着，又开始狂笑，大步走向了那个同样落魄的老头。
en: You stand frozen before the puddle of mud. Under the eaves of a nearby wineshop, you spot Zheng Qian — Doctor of the Broad Learning Academy at the Imperial Directorate. He is lining up a few rusted copper coins on the counter, exchanging them for a corner's worth of the cheapest cloudy wine. A gust of wind blows past. You once thought his patched but washed-to-fading blue robe was the "principled purity" posturing of a famous scholar — until this moment, when you see him shiver uncontrollably in the cold wind, yet still carefully shield that cheap, chipped inkstick in his breast with his sleeve.

zh: 郑虔转过头，看到了浑身泥水、失魂落魄的你，也看到了地上的残稿。他没有问你考得如何，也没有丝毫的怜悯。他只是笑着扬了扬手里的酒葫芦，朝你招手：【子美！愣着干嘛？今夜金吾不禁，这上等的酸米酒，我请客！】
en: You hesitate for a moment, force a smile, then break into raucous laughter and stride toward that equally down-and-out old man.

zh: 目送他的背影消失在黑暗中...
en: Zheng Qian turns around and sees you — covered in mud, utterly dejected — and also sees the ruined drafts on the ground. He does not ask how the exam went, nor does he show any pity. He simply grins, raises his wine gourd, and beckons to you: "Zimei! What are you standing there for? The night watch is suspended tonight — this premium sour rice wine is on me!"

zh: 酒的辛辣在胃里渐渐褪去，却奇迹般地抵御了春夜的死寒。上元节的喧闹已近尾声，长街上满是被踩烂的灯笼纸。郑虔拍了拍你的肩膀，裹紧那件单薄的青衫，摇摇晃晃地走入了没有灯光的暗巷。\\n\\n'子美，这长安的月亮，在哪看都一样。' 他没有劝你留下，也没有劝你离开。
en: You watch his silhouette disappear into the darkness...

zh: [未解锁] 捡起烂泥里的残稿。也许明天去右相府门前长跪不起，哪怕只求个幕僚的位子……
en: The bite of the wine gradually fades in your stomach, yet miraculously it has warded off the deadly chill of the spring night. The Lantern Festival revelry is winding down; the main street is littered with crushed lantern paper. Zheng Qian pats your shoulder, wraps his thin blue robe tighter, and staggers into an unlit alley.\n\n"Zimei, the moon over Chang'an looks the same no matter where you see it." He did not urge you to stay, nor did he urge you to leave.

zh: 天大笑，将残酒猛地泼在那团烂泥般的诗稿上。去他娘的野无遗贤！
en: [Locked] Pick up the ruined drafts from the mud. Perhaps tomorrow you'll go kneel before the Chancellor's gate — even if it's just for a staff advisor post...

zh: 你独自站在冷风中。左手是那团糊满烂泥的干谒诗稿，右手是空荡荡的酒碗。过去的三年，你就像一台精确的机器，每天在那些朱门前计算着笑容的弧度和弯腰的角度。现在，你看着地上相国府马车留下的深深车辙，那股支撑着你的发条……好像断了。
en: He laughs wildly at the heavens and splashes the dregs of his wine onto the mud-caked poems. To hell with "No talent left unrecognized in the wild!"

zh: 一阵寒风吹过，你猛地干呕起来。你的胃和你的脊梁比理智更早做出了决定——你已经无法强迫自己的双膝再弯下去了。(未解锁，正式版解锁）
en: You stand alone in the cold wind. In your left hand: that lump of mud-caked patronage poems. In your right: an empty wine bowl. For the past three years, you've been like a precision machine, calibrating the arc of your smile and the angle of your bow before those vermilion gates each day. Now, staring at the deep wheel ruts left by the Chancellor's carriage, the mainspring that has been driving you... seems to have snapped.

zh: 你心性的稳固程度。定力越高，承受的伤害越小，但兴致起伏也变得平缓，更沉静内敛。
en: A cold gust blows past, and you suddenly retch. Your stomach and your spine reached a verdict before your reason did — you can no longer force your knees to bend. (Locked — available in the full release)
The steadiness of your mind. The higher your composure, the less damage you take — but your emotional swings also grow milder, more restrained and introspective.
Unmoved by the eight winds — your heart is like bedrock.
Undisturbed by external things — the mirror of your heart is spotless.
Ripples stir on the lake of your heart.
Your spirit shatters — all hope turns to ash.
Mind like a restless monkey, will like a galloping horse.
Unmoved even if Mount Tai crumbles before you.

zh: 你随意吟了几句，觉得不成体统，也就搁下了。

en: You casually recite a few lines, feel they lack any proper form, and set the brush aside.

zh: 从八品下小官，月薪两斗麦

en: A Junior Eighth-Rank, Lower Grade petty official — monthly salary: two pecks of wheat.

zh: 一旦你的寿命到达，你会死！
en: Imperial Decree: Ministry of Personnel Appointment
Once your lifespan runs out, you will die!
You are merely an ordinary person.
You've eaten a lot of protein powder.

zh: 也罢\n登高本为遣兴，今日既无此心，强求反而不美。凭栏远眺，云低风急，不如归去。

en: So be it.\nYou climbed to dispel melancholy, but today your heart is simply not in it — forcing it would spoil the mood. Leaning on the railing, you gaze out: clouds hang low, the wind is urgent. Better to go home.

zh: 失足\n登至半途，脚下碎石松动，一个趔趄险些跌倒。虽无大碍，却也失了兴致，只得悻悻下山。

en: A Misstep\nHalfway up, loose gravel shifts beneath your feet — you stumble and nearly fall. Though unhurt, your spirit is dampened, and you descend the mountain in dejection.

zh: 登高\n乐游原上秋风猎猎，天高云淡。你登至高处，俯瞰长安城郭如棋盘，胸中块垒为之一舒。

en: Climbing High\nOn Leyou Plateau the autumn wind whistles — the sky is high, the clouds are thin. You ascend to the summit and look down upon Chang'an's city walls laid out like a chessboard, the knot in your chest loosening at last.

zh: 兴尽\n曲江池畔游人如织，喧闹不堪。本想寻一处清静，却被嘈杂扰了心境，兴致索然，转身离去。

en: Joy Fades\nBy Qujiang Pool, the crowds press thick as woven silk, the clamor unbearable. You'd hoped to find a quiet corner, but the din frays your nerves. Interest spent, you turn and leave.

zh: 游春\n曲江池畔春色正浓，烟柳画桥，游人如织。你沿池漫步，看碧波荡漾，听莺啼燕语，心神为之一畅。

en: Spring Outing\nBy Qujiang Pool, spring is at its peak — mist-veiled willows, painted bridges, crowds thick as brocade. You stroll along the bank, watching emerald waves ripple, listening to orioles and swallows call. Your spirit lifts.

zh: 荒原\n登上少陵原，满目荒草萋萋，断碑残垣散落其间。想起昔年在此吟咏的前辈，而今安在？不觉悲从中来。

en: Barrens\nYou climb Shaoling Yuan. Before you, wild grass stretches everywhere, broken stelae and crumbling walls scattered among them. You think of the elders who once composed verses here — where are they now? Sorrow rises unbidden.

zh: 登高\n少陵原上秋草萋萋，你登至高处凭吊古迹。断碑残垣间，依稀可见前朝题刻，不觉神游千载，诗兴勃发。

en: Ascending\nAutumn grass grows thick on Shaoling Yuan. You climb to the highest point to pay respects to the ruins. Among broken stelae and toppled walls, faint traces of past dynasties' inscriptions remain. Your mind wanders across a thousand years — poetic inspiration surges.

zh: 风雨骤至，郊原路断，苍天不与人便
en: Amid towers and terraces, one forgets this fleeting life a while.
Wind and rain strike without warning, the country roads cut off — Heaven grants no convenience.

zh: 指节冻伤，屈伸不利，皮肉青紫。

en: Finger joints frostbitten, stiff to bend or straighten, the flesh bruised purple.

zh: 指尖坏死，皮肉焦黑如炭，关节锁死，痛觉尽失。

en: Fingertips necrotic, flesh charred black like coal, joints locked solid, all sensation of pain gone.

zh: 肺气已损，咳血不止，形销骨立。

en: Lung qi damaged, ceaseless bloody coughing, body wasted to skin and bone.

zh: 风寒入体，头痛身热，咳嗽不止。

en: Wind-cold invades the body — head aches, fever burns, coughing will not stop.

zh: 意象耗尽，风寒入骨。健康流失速度倍增。

en: Imagery exhausted — wind-cold seeps into the bone. Health loss rate doubled.

zh: 意象耗尽，心神俱损。每旬流失生命，行动上限永久削减。

en: Imagery exhausted — both heart and spirit wounded. Lose life each ten-day period; maximum actions permanently reduced.

zh: 宦海浮沉，壮志难酬，心中郁结难解

en: Tossed on the bureaucratic sea, grand ambitions unfulfilled — the knot in your chest refuses to loosen.

zh: 狂言谵语，不避亲疏，形神皆乱。

en: Wild talk and delirious ravings, making no distinction between kin and stranger — both body and mind in chaos.

zh: 仰头饮尽最后一碗。碗底朝天，一滴不剩。
酒旗在风里拍得猎猎作响。你推开那扇半掩的门，酒保看你一眼便不再说话——他认得这种眼神。你要了最烈的那种，不是品，是灌。每一口下去，昨日在权贵门前的记忆就淡一分。酒坛见底时，昨夜那张谄媚的嘴脸终于开始模糊——像墨迹在水里散开。你不记得付了多少钱，只记得走出门时，长安的月光刺得眼睛发酸。
en: You tilt your head back and drain the last bowl. The bowl faces the sky — not a drop remains.

The tavern banner snaps and crackles in the wind. You push open the half-closed door. The barkeeper glances at you and says nothing — he knows that look. You order the strongest they have, not to savor but to pour down. With each gulp, yesterday's memories before the gates of power fade a shade. When the jar runs dry, last night's fawning face finally begins to blur — like ink spreading in water. You can't remember how much you paid, only that when you stepped outside, Chang'an's moonlight stung your eyes.

zh: 天宝六载秋科举，若叩不开这扇门，你的一身才华，终将沦为盛世的笑柄。
你想齐家治国平天下，而这需要以跃入体制为前提。带着半生心血的行卷，你站到了长安的朱门之外。权贵的手指缝里，漏下的是天下士子的命运。
en: The imperial exam of the autumn of Tianbao Year 6. If you cannot pry open this door, all your talent will become nothing but a laughingstock in this golden age.

You wish to regulate the family, govern the state, and bring peace to all under Heaven — yet this requires plunging into the system first. Clutching a portfolio of half a lifetime's work, you stand before the vermilion gates of Chang'an. Between the fingers of the powerful slips the fate of every scholar in the empire.

zh: 「状态」长安布衣。相府的门房连正眼都不会看你。长安城的名利场里，查无此人。
「状态」名动公卿。你的干谒诗已被多位权贵传阅。只要再多送些盘缠，补上几首好诗，似乎就只差那临门一脚了
en: [Status] A commoner of Chang'an. The gatekeepers of the Chancellor's mansion won't even look you in the eye. In this city's arena of fame and fortune, you simply do not exist.

zh: 窃比稷契。相国已向你许下重诺。你自认才华已比肩上古贤相稷与契，立登要路津，就在今朝！
en: [Status] A name whispered among the nobility. Your petitioning poems have circulated among several powerful figures. Send a little more silver, offer a few more fine verses, and it seems you're but a single kick from the goal.

zh: 酒肆中人来人往，你侧耳听了半晌，却都是些家长里短的闲话。掌柜收了酒钱，用抹布敷衍地擦了一下桌面，什么新鲜事也没有。
en: Daring to compare yourself to Ji and Xie. The Chancellor has made you a weighty promise. In your own eyes, your talent now rivals the sage ministers of antiquity. A swift ascent to the key posts — today is the day!

The tavern bustles with comings and goings. You strain your ears for a good while, but it's all household gossip and small talk. The innkeeper takes your money, wipes the table with a perfunctory swipe of a rag — nothing newsworthy at all.

zh: 酒肆角落，一桌客人压低了声音在谈——{@imaginary_gain_hint}。你端着杯，装作看窗外的雨，耳朵却一字不漏地收着。说者无心，听者有意，这倒是意外所得。

en: In a corner of the tavern, a table of patrons speaks in lowered voices — {@imaginary_gain_hint}. You hold your cup, pretending to watch the rain beyond the window, but your ears catch every word. The speakers meant nothing by it, but the listener took note — an unexpected gain.

zh: 药酒葫芦见了底，可身上的毒症却纹丝不动。这药方，怕是不对症。

en: The medicinal wine gourd is empty, but the poison in your body hasn't budged. This prescription, you fear, is not the right one.

zh: 从袖中取出药酒葫芦，仰头灌下一口。药味辛辣，入腹却化作一股暖流，身上的毒症似乎轻了几分。

en: You draw the medicinal wine gourd from your sleeve, tilt your head back, and take a swig. The herbal taste is sharp, but once it settles in your belly it turns into a warm current — the poison afflicting you seems to ease a little.

zh: 杯中之酒寡淡如水，喝了半日也不见暖意。这酒怕是掺了水，白花了银钱。

en: The wine in your cup is as bland as water. You've been drinking half the afternoon without the slightest warmth. This wine has surely been watered down — silver wasted.

zh: 拈起酒杯，浅浅抿了一口。酒水温润入喉，微醺之际，只觉得身上轻快了些许。

en: You lift the wine cup and take a shallow sip. The wine glides down warm and smooth. In this gentle tipsiness, you feel your body grow a little lighter.
A Quiet Drink Soothes the Heart

zh: 酒瓮见底，四邻沽尽，无处可得一滴
en: Doors shut, guests turned away — hiding from the world in wine.
The wine jar runs dry, every neighbor has sold out — not a single drop to be found anywhere.

zh: 相国府的后门也对你关上了。
en: The gate guard didn't even glance at you.

zh: 你发现自己连打点下人的铜钱都没了...
en: Even the back door of the Chancellor's mansion has closed to you.
You realize you don't even have the copper coins to bribe the servants anymore...

zh: 磨墨，在卷首郑重写下你的名字
长安的物价贵得令人咋舌。你在城南偏僻的客舍里租下了一张散发着霉味的床榻，点燃了身上最后半截劣质的残烛。案几上，是你准备投递给当朝右相李林甫的诗文。夜风透窗，烛火摇晃得让人心慌。窗外的萤火虫闪烁，好像暗示着你，和你的才华的命运
en: Grind the ink, and solemnly write your name at the head of the scroll.

The prices in Chang'an are eye-watering. You rent a mold-scented cot in a remote hostel south of the city and light the last half-stump of your cheapest candle. On the desk lie the poems and essays you plan to submit to Chancellor Li Linfu. Night wind seeps through the window; the candle flame flickers and fills you with unease. Fireflies blink outside — as though hinting at the fate awaiting you and your talent.

zh: 你决定回家看看。一路从东门灞桥出，到骊山，强渡渭河。再到奉先县

en: You decide to go home for a visit. You set out from Ba Bridge at the eastern gate, pass Mount Li, force a crossing of the Wei River, and press on to Fengxian County.

zh: 你本能地跑向最近的一处朱门屋檐下避雨。
正午。第一滴雨砸在你袖口的墨迹上。紧接着是倾盆大雨。一辆紫盖马车从朱雀大街疾驰而过，泥水劈头盖脸浇透了你的白袍。
en: Instinctively, you dash toward the nearest vermilion gate and take shelter under its eaves.

zh: 银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
en: Noon. The first raindrop slams onto the ink stain at your cuff. Then the sky opens. A carriage with a violet canopy thunders down Vermilion Bird Avenue, drenching your white robe from head to foot in muddy water.
Like a silver vase shattering, water and slurry burst forth — like iron cavalry charging, blades and spears ring out.

zh: 一队戴着傩面具的舞者欢呼着冲进人群。你被重重地撞在肩膀上，摔倒在青石板上。怀里那卷写满治国策论和干谒诗的卷轴滚落进了地上的水坑里。
一只穿着丝绸锦履的脚踩在了卷轴上。紧接着是第二只、第三只。欢笑的人群从你身边涌过。当你再抽回卷轴时，上面的字迹已经和泥水糊成了一团黑泥。
en: A troupe of dancers wearing Nuo masks cheers and charges into the crowd. A shoulder slams hard into you, and you crash onto the flagstones. The scroll in your arms — covered with statecraft essays and petition poems — rolls into a puddle on the ground.

A foot in embroidered silk brocade steps on the scroll. Then a second, then a third. The laughing crowd surges past you. When you finally pull the scroll back, the writing has mingled with mud into a black sludge.

zh: 砰！朱门半开，一根水火棍猛地杵在你的胸口，将你推入雨中。【滚远点，别脏了相府的台阶！】
en: Stumbling and staggering, you flee into a dark alley.
Bang! The vermilion gate swings half-open. A guard's staff rams hard into your chest, shoving you back into the rain. [Get lost — don't dirty the Chancellor's steps!]

zh: 你顺着人流走入西市。胡姬在酒肆二楼撒下花瓣，杂耍艺人喷出的火龙照亮了半条街。羊肉汤的浓烈香气直往鼻子里钻，你的胃里发出一阵痉挛的绞痛。路边的汤饼摊正冒着热气。
en: You reach for the pouch at your waist...

zh: 褡裢里空空如也。为了打点考官和干谒权贵，你已经花光了最后一文铜钱。摊主原本堆笑的脸瞬间冷了下来，用抹布猛地一甩桌子：【不吃别挡道！】
en: You follow the crowd into the Western Market. Foreign dancing girls scatter flower petals from a tavern's second floor. A street performer breathes a dragon of fire that lights up half the street. The rich aroma of mutton soup drills into your nostrils — your stomach convulses with a spasm of hunger. A noodle stall on the roadside steams invitingly.

zh: 靠在湿冷的墙壁上，直到雨停...
en: The pouch is empty. To grease the examiners and petition the powerful, you have spent your very last copper coin. The vendor's smiling face freezes instantly. He snaps his rag against the table: [If you're not eating, get out of the way!]

zh: 你跌入屋背后的暗巷。这里积水没过脚踝，混合着腐烂的菜叶和马粪味。一个蜷缩在草席下的流民递过来半块发黑的胡饼：“别饿死了”。你下意识地想要摆手拒绝，却借着闪电，看清了自己伸出去的手——指甲缝里塞满黑泥，袖口破裂，比那流民好不到哪去
en: You lean against the cold, wet wall and wait for the rain to stop...

zh: 老天...我怎么没发现这里有这么多穷人？
en: You stumble into the alley behind the houses. Here, standing water rises past your ankles, mixed with the stench of rotting vegetable leaves and horse dung. A vagrant huddled under a straw mat holds out half a blackened flatbread: "Don't starve to death." Instinctively, you raise a hand to refuse — but a flash of lightning reveals your outstretched hand: nails clogged with black grime, sleeves torn. You're no better off than the vagrant.
Heavens... how did I never notice there were so many poor people here?

zh: 雨停时已是入夜。远处的坊门没有像往常一样关闭。今夜是上元灯节，金吾不禁。漫天的红灯笼亮了起来。

en: By the time the rain stops, night has fallen. The ward gates in the distance have not closed as usual. Tonight is the Lantern Festival — the imperial guard stands down. A skyful of red lanterns begins to glow.

zh: 你正拧干袖子上的泥水...
朱门宏大，辉煌。金色的檐角在雨中熠熠生辉，屋檐宽大的站三个人都绰绰有余。可能是因为才下雨，这里只有你一个人。你终于可以气定神闲的站在朱门下躲雨，就像以前常做的那样
en: You are wringing muddy water from your sleeves...

The vermilion gate is grand, resplendent. Its gilded eaves gleam in the rain, broad enough to shelter three men with room to spare. Perhaps because it just rained, you're alone here. At last you can stand composed beneath the vermilion gate and wait out the rain — just as you used to do.

zh: 对方等待着你先出一首诗
en: A Distant Guest at the Vermilion Gate
The other party waits for you to compose the first poem.

zh: 你来到门前，家仆通报后回话说主人身体不适，这三旬概不见客。你只得转身离去。

en: You arrive at the gate. The servant relays your greeting and returns with word that the master is unwell and will receive no guests for the next three ten-day periods. You can only turn and leave.
Died when the body could no longer hold on.

zh: 你死了，但你的痛苦也结束了。你不再需要为家人而担忧，你不再需要为百姓而痛苦：你死了，它带走了你的痛苦，忧患，才气和人格。

en: You are dead, but your suffering has ended too. No more worrying about your family, no more anguish for the common people. You died — and death took your pain, your cares, your talent, and your character with it.

zh: 在乱世不知道被谁所杀。这个世道？你自己？

en: Killed by someone unknown in these chaotic times. By this age? By yourself?

zh: 你死了，你变成了一具尸体，这样不是坏的，在乱世中反而可能是最好的结局

en: You are dead, reduced to a corpse. This is not a bad thing — in times of chaos, it may in fact be the best possible ending.

zh: 此事件应从屏幕底部向上滑入。选择确认后无副作用，后续事件回归正常（默认顶部滑入）。
纸带从底部滑入 —— 动画策略测试成功。
en: This event should slide in from the bottom of the screen. Choosing Confirm has no side effects; subsequent events return to normal (default top slide-in).

zh: 纸带测试 · 下方滑入
en: Paper strip slides in from the bottom — animation strategy test successful.

zh: 你主动示好，对方有些意外，对你多了几分善意。

en: You take the initiative to befriend them. The other party is somewhat surprised and shows you a bit more goodwill.

zh: 你以逢迎之道交好，对方欣然接纳。

en: You court their favor with flattery and charm — the other party gladly accepts.

zh: 你以狂客之姿示好，对方不敢怠慢。

en: You approach with the swagger of an unrestrained eccentric — the other party dares not slight you.

zh: 你以钻营之道结交，对方见有利可图，态度热切。

en: You befriend them through opportunistic channels. Seeing profit to be had, the other party's attitude turns enthusiastic.
"Ten years of study by the cold window — everything rides on this moment!"

zh: 恭敬地递上行卷，并在下面压上你大半的盘缠
en: Spring of Tianbao Year 6 — the day of the grand examination.

zh: 右相府的朱门比你想象的还要高耸。出乎意料，接待你的并非粗鄙的门卫，而是一位衣着考究的相府主簿。他面带春风般的微笑，甚至命人给你端来了一杯温度恰到好处的茶水。主簿修长的手指不经意地将银钱拨入袖中，随手翻开你的行卷瞥了一眼首联。'好字。'他赞许地点点头，'杜公子的才情，在下必定如实禀报相爷。回去静候佳音吧。
en: You respectfully present your portfolio, slipping most of your travel money underneath.

zh: 你走出相府，秋风微凉，但你的内心却已被这句客套话点燃了熊熊烈火。
en: The vermilion gate of the Right Chancellor's mansion is even more towering than you imagined. To your surprise, it is not a coarse gate guard who receives you, but an elegantly dressed chief clerk of the household. He wears a spring-breeze smile and even orders a cup of perfectly warm tea brought out for you. His slender fingers casually sweep the silver into his sleeve as he leafs through your portfolio and glances at the opening couplet. "Fine calligraphy." He nods approvingly. "Master Du's talent — I shall report it faithfully to His Excellency the Chancellor. Return home and await good news."
You walk out of the Chancellor's mansion. The autumn wind is cool, but your heart has been set ablaze by those polite words.
First Visit to the Chancellor's Mansion

zh: 获得从八品官，月薪两斗米

en: Awarded a Junior Eighth-Rank official post, with a monthly salary of two dou of rice.

zh: 你站在长安的明德门外，抬头望着这座被盛世狂热笼罩的庞大都城。你的行囊里没有多少盘缠，只有一卷你自认足以惊动天下公卿的诗稿。
en: Stepping into Chang'an to seek your place in the world.

You stand outside Chang'an's Mingde Gate, looking up at this vast capital swathed in the fevered glow of a golden age. Your traveling pack holds little silver — only a scroll of poems you believe sufficient to stir every duke and minister under Heaven.
Tianbao Year 4 — First Entry into Chang'an

zh: 天宝四年，秋。你默念着自己的诗句，带着这股想要致君尧舜上的狂妄，一头撞进了这座权力的迷宫。
en: "I deemed myself rather outstanding, certain to swiftly ascend to the key posts."

zh: 但长安的盛世太过喧嚣...
en: Autumn of Tianbao Year 4. Murmuring your own verses under your breath, carrying this arrogant ambition to guide the sovereign to sagehood, you plunge headlong into this labyrinth of power.

zh: 根本没人听得见，一个异乡人的野心。
en: But the golden age of Chang'an is far too loud...
No one can hear the ambition of a stranger from the provinces.

zh: 旬末结算，囊中已无一文钱。客栈老板骂骂咧咧地将你赶出门外，寒风中你蜷缩在街角……

en: At the end of the ten-day period, your purse is empty. The innkeeper curses and throws you out. In the cold wind, you huddle in a street corner...

zh: 你掌握了对方的把柄，是交好还是威胁？

en: You hold leverage over the other party. Befriend them, or threaten them?

zh: 你暗中查访，掌握了对方的一个把柄。

en: You investigate discreetly and obtain a piece of leverage over the other party.

zh: 对方嗤笑一声，你的威胁软弱无力，如同蝼蚁撼树。

en: The other party scoffs — your threat is weak and futile, like an ant trying to shake a tree.

zh: 逢迎者八面玲珑，你的威胁如石沉大海。

en: The flatterer is smooth in every direction — your threat sinks like a stone in the sea.

zh: 你隐晦地暗示手中的把柄，对方神情一紧。

en: You subtly hint at the leverage you hold. The other party's expression tightens.

zh: 狂客本性狷狂，你的威胁如烈火烹油。

en: The wild eccentric is unrestrained by nature — your threat is like pouring oil onto a blazing fire.

zh: 抓住了对方的痛处，对方冷汗涔涔，不得不服软。
en: Hmph. Good that you know fear.
You've seized their sore spot. The other party breaks out in a cold sweat and has no choice but to yield.

zh: 钻营者利益至上，你的威胁正中软肋。

en: The opportunist puts profit above all — your threat strikes right at their weak point.

zh: 白忙\n搬了半日砖，累得腰酸背痛。到黄昏找工头结账，他却皱眉道：「今日主家没给钱，改日再来。」一句改日，不知又是何日。

en: Wasted Labor\nYou haul bricks for half a day until your back aches and your muscles scream. At dusk you find the foreman to settle up, but he frowns and says, "The master didn't pay today. Come back another time." "Another time" — who knows when that will be.

zh: 搬砖今日市口热闹，工头见你膀大腰圆，招手便唤：「来得好！正缺人手。」你扛了几趟砖石，虽汗流浃背，倒也挣得几文铜钱。

en: The market is bustling today. The foreman, seeing your stout build, waves you over: "Right on time! We're short-handed." You haul several loads of bricks and stone. Though drenched in sweat, you earn a few copper coins for your trouble.

zh: 市井无声\n坊间寂寥，商贩稀疏，偶有过客也是行色匆匆。无甚可看之处，不如归去翻翻书卷。

en: A Silent Market\nThe ward is desolate, vendors few and far between. The occasional passerby hurries along without a glance. Nothing worth seeing here — better to go home and leaf through a book.

zh: 知音稀\n有人驻足看了半晌，你以为是知音，却听他道：「这字写得倒是有力，可惜不似王右军。」你苦笑——世人只知右军，哪知天地之大，岂止一家？

en: Few True Connoisseurs\nSomeone stops and studies your work for a long moment. You think you've found a kindred spirit — until he says, "These characters are forceful, yes, but they don't resemble Wang Xizhi's." You force a bitter smile. The world knows only the Sage of Calligraphy — who realizes that between Heaven and Earth, there is room for more than one master?

zh: 卖字\n你带着近日最得意的一幅字来到东市，寻了个显眼的位置挂起来。有识货的文人驻足良久，最终点头掏钱——虽不多，却是知音之价。
en: A Kindred Ear Is Hard to Find

Selling Calligraphy\nYou bring your most prized recent piece to the Eastern Market and hang it in a conspicuous spot. A discerning scholar stops, studies it at length, and finally nods, reaching for his purse. Not much silver — but it is the price of a true connoisseur.

zh: 市侩\n摆了一上午摊，好不容易来了个问价的，却是个附庸风雅的商人。嫌你字「不够工整」，只肯出三文钱的润笔费，气得你收摊走人。

en: Vulgar Haggler\nYou've kept your stall all morning. At last someone comes to ask the price — a merchant playing at refinement. He complains your calligraphy is "not neat enough" and offers a mere three copper coins for your brushwork. Furious, you pack up and leave.

zh: 卖字\n铺开宣纸，研墨挥毫，写了三两幅字挂在摊前。有路人驻足看了看，掏出几文钱买去——虽不识草隶行楷，倒也图个新鲜。

en: Selling Calligraphy\nYou spread out rice paper, grind ink, and wield the brush, producing two or three pieces to hang at your stall. A passerby stops, looks, and fishes out a few coins to buy one. They can't tell cursive from clerical from running script — but it's a novelty, at least.

zh: 无人问津\n你辗转几个歌坊递上新词，皆被婉拒——「这位先生的诗，不合时下的调子」。你只得将诗稿收回袖中。

en: No One Inquires\nYou go from one song house to another offering your new verses, but each politely declines — "This gentleman's poems don't suit the current fashion." You can only tuck the manuscript back into your sleeve.

zh: 平康坊传唱\n你将诗稿递入平康坊。数日后，坊中歌女竟已在传唱你的新词——虽只卖了几个铜板，但曲声穿过帘栊，落在行人的耳边。

en: Sung in Pingkang Ward\nYou slip your poems into Pingkang Ward. Days later, the courtesans there are already singing your new verses. The sale brought only a few copper coins, but the melody slips through the curtains and falls upon the ears of passersby.

zh: 试药\n掌柜的递来一碗新配的汤药，说是大补之方。你喝下去只觉得腹中翻腾，冷汗涔涔，半天缓不过气来——这药怕是配错了。

en: Testing Medicine\nThe apothecary hands you a bowl of freshly brewed decoction, claiming it's a potent tonic. You drink it down — your stomach immediately churns, cold sweat pours from you, and you spend half the day gasping for breath. This medicine must have been wrongly prepared.

zh: 试药\n掌柜的递来一碗新配的汤药，说是补气血的方子。你仰头喝下，药性平和，倒无不适。掌柜满意地点点头，从柜下摸出几枚铜钱递来。

en: Testing Medicine\nThe shopkeeper hands you a bowl of freshly prepared herbal brew, claiming it nourishes the blood and qi. You tilt your head back and drink. The medicine is mild, causing no discomfort. The shopkeeper nods with satisfaction and fishes out a few copper coins from beneath the counter, handing them to you.

zh: 适逢某公忌日，长安罢市，百肆紧闭

en: It happens to be the death anniversary of a certain dignitary. Chang'an's markets are shuttered, every shop bolted shut.

zh: 里正还坐在那张磨得发亮的木凳上，像是从未挪过。你走过去的时候，他正[glitch level=6]闭着眼[/glitch]晒太阳——不，也许只是在打盹。冬天的太阳没有温度，照在他脸上像一层薄灰。
里正闭着眼，指了一个你根本不认识的方向。风里…听不到哭声了。
en: The village head still sits on that wooden stool, its surface worn glossy, as if he had never moved. When you approach, he has his eyes [glitch level=6]closed[/glitch], basking in the sun — no, perhaps just dozing. The winter sun carries no warmth; it lies on his face like a thin layer of ash.
Eyes still shut, the village head points in a direction you don't recognize at all. In the wind… you can no longer hear the crying.

zh: 我怎么对这个地方一点都不熟悉
en: The Village Head at the Entrance
Why does this place feel so utterly unfamiliar

zh: 你凭着十年前的记忆在这片田野里摸索。路早就被荒草吞没了大半，但方向还在骨头里。风从奉先县城那边吹过来，夹着一股[glitch]柴̧̧̱̰̣̱̈̄̃̇́̀́̄烟̄̂̈̆̂̇̌̀[/glitch]味。
en: Turn Back to the Village Entrance

zh: 远处的茅草屋里传来婴儿断断续续的啼哭，像是在硬撑。
en: You grope through the fields, relying on memories from a decade ago. The path has long been swallowed by wild grass, but its direction still lives in your bones. The wind blows over from Fengxian county town, carrying a whiff of [glitch]f̈̄̃̇í̀́̄ŗ̧̱̰̣̱ē̂̈̆̂̇̌̀ẅ̄̃̇́̀́̄o̧̧̱̰̣̱ō̂̈̆̂̇̌̀d[/glitch] smoke.
From a distant thatched hut comes the intermittent cry of a baby, as if struggling to hold on.

zh: 你回到村头，察看着四周

en: You return to the village entrance and survey your surroundings

zh: 门虚掩着。你推开门，屋里的霉味混着一股甜腻的腐烂气息迎面扑来。地上趴着一具[glitch level=4]干尸[/glitch]——骨节粗大，肩宽，不像女人，更不是孩子。你蹲下来翻看尸体的手，指节上有老茧，是握锄头的痕迹。
你急疯了，在泥水里跌跌撞撞。那阵哭声变得极其微弱，几乎要被风声盖过。
en: The door is ajar. You push it open. A musty odor mixed with a cloying sweetness of decay hits your face. On the floor lies a [glitch level=4]desiccated corpse[/glitch] — thick-knuckled, broad-shouldered. Not a woman, certainly not a child. You crouch down and turn over the hand. Calloused knuckles. The marks of a hoe.
Mad with desperation, you stumble through the mud. The crying has grown terribly faint, nearly swallowed by the wind.

zh: 沿着记忆中的小径，去找十年前住过的那间屋
回头去找村口的里正，他应该知道这些年发生了什么
en: Follow the path in your memory to find the house you lived in ten years ago

en: Go back and find the village head at the entrance; he should know what happened these years

zh: 你站在奉先村的村口，风从骊山方向灌过来，把衣摆吹得猎猎作响。十年前的记忆在脑子里乱撞，每条巷子都像，又都不像。村口的老槐树还在，但树下的石凳上坐着陌生的人。
en: Don't ask anyone — trust your instincts to find that leaky old house

You stand at the entrance of Fengxian village. The wind barrels in from the direction of Mount Li, whipping your robes with a snapping sound. Memories from ten years ago crash through your mind — every alley looks right and wrong at the same time. The old locust tree at the entrance still stands, but strangers now sit on the stone bench beneath it.
You don't know where home is

en: Head Toward the Small Wooden Hut

en: You stand at the village entrance again. The wind still comes from Mount Li, but now you know — some things are no longer the same. The village head is dead. The area where you once lived has changed beyond recognition — they seem to have relocated somewhere unfamiliar. You rarely come back, and you have no money. Over the years, the village has become a foreign place to you.

zh: 你知道那里不对，里正死了，他们似乎搬迁到了你不熟悉的地方
en: You know something is wrong. The village head is dead, and they seem to have relocated somewhere you don't recognize.

zh: 文思枯涩，笔端如坠千钧，纸上空无一字

en: Your literary thoughts run dry and coarse. The brush-tip feels weighed down by a thousand pounds. The paper remains blank — not a single word.

zh: 你带着这几年在长安四处干谒换来的微薄名望，深吸一口气，跨过贡院高高的门槛。阳光洒在你的白袍上，你觉得大唐的未来就在你笔下。

en: Carrying the meager reputation you've scraped together from years of petitioning officials across Chang'an, you draw a deep breath and step over the Examination Hall's towering threshold. Sunlight falls upon your white robes. You feel that the future of the Great Tang lies beneath your brush.

zh: 针砭时弊：言明边镇兵权过重，朝堂言路闭塞。
违心作答：“右相调理阴阳，海内晏清，真乃千古贤相！”
en: Criticize the current abuses: Argue that border garrisons hold excessive military power and the court has stifled all channels of honest counsel.

zh: 考官死死盯着你的笔尖。你敢写下半个字，今天就别想活着走出贡院。
en: Answer against your conscience: "The Grand Chancellor harmonizes yin and yang; the realm is at peace under his governance. Truly a sage minister for the ages!"
The examiner fixes his stare on the tip of your brush. Write so much as half a character of dissent, and you won't leave this examination hall alive today.

zh: 试卷的第二题并非诗词经义，而是策问：“今圣上垂拱而治，右相理政，天下如何？”你握紧了笔，冷汗滴在纸上。主考官（李林甫的心腹）在走道里来回巡视，眼神阴冷。
en: A wave of nausea rises in your stomach

The second question on the exam paper is not about poetry or the classics — it's a policy essay: "His Majesty governs through effortless virtue while the Grand Chancellor administers the realm. How fares the empire?" You grip your brush tighter; cold sweat drips onto the paper. The chief examiner — Li Linfu's trusted man — paces the aisles, his gaze dark and cold.

zh: 天宝六年，贡院放榜。你满怀信心地挤入人群，寻找自己的名字。
没有。不仅没有你，你认识的所有才子，郑虔、高适……全都不在榜上.
en: In the sixth year of Tianbao, the Examination Hall posts its results. Full of confidence, you squeeze into the crowd, searching for your name.

zh: 相国李林甫上表贺皇帝：‘天下英才尽入彀中，野无遗贤。’
en: Nothing. Not just you — every talented scholar you know — Zheng Qian, Gao Shi… none of them are on the list.
Grand Chancellor Li Linfu submits a memorial congratulating the Emperor: "All the empire's talents have been gathered into the fold. No worthy man remains outside the court."
A Long Road Ahead — Return Home

zh: 你的生命之本。健康越低，行动越受限。低于20将触发濒死危机。

en: The root of your life force. The lower your health, the more restricted your actions become. Falling below 20 triggers a life-threatening crisis.
Reborn anew — no ailment can touch you
Sickness crashes down like a mountain

zh: 宴席之上，玉盘珍馐，觥筹交错。你端着酒杯在人群中穿梭，试图与几位说得上话的人物攀谈。然而这些贵人要么被更显赫的宾客包围，要么对你只是敷衍地点头寒暄便转身而去。夜深宴散，朱门在身后吱呀关上。你立在阶下，望着一地狼藉的残烛，心中空落落的。这重金购得的入席券，终究没有换来一句承诺。

en: At the banquet, jade platters bear rare delicacies, wine cups cross in festive toasts. You navigate through the crowd, cup in hand, attempting to strike up conversation with several figures of influence. Yet these dignitaries are either surrounded by more prominent guests or merely offer you a perfunctory nod before turning away. Night deepens; the feast disperses. The vermilion gates creak shut behind you. Standing beneath the steps, gazing at the scattered remains of spent candles, emptiness fills your chest. The seat at this table, bought at great cost, has yielded not a single promise.

zh: 朱门之内，灯火辉煌。你与{@npc_name}相谈甚欢，从他的言谈中你感受到此人虽素未谋面，却在长安城中颇有根基。宴罢，{@npc_name}从袖中取出一封亲笔书信递给你，以作引荐之资。
en: The Feast Ends — The Guests Vanish

Within the vermilion gates, lanterns blaze bright. You share warm conversation with {@npc_name}; from his manner of speech you sense that though you've never met before, this man has substantial connections in Chang'an. As the feast concludes, {@npc_name} draws a personally written letter from his sleeve and hands it to you — a token of introduction.
Would rather keep company with common market folk

As if aided by the divine — a thousand words flow from the brush
Unable to set brush to paper — heart and mind adrift

en: You crouched in a corner of the dark alley the entire night, your legs numb and stiff, dew soaking through your robes. Figures passed by the alley mouth again and again, but not a single one stopped. The night watchman's clapper sounded three times; the eastern sky was already tinged with the pale white of dawn. You rose, dusted yourself off — a whole night's effort and a few bits of silver, all for nothing. The secrets of Chang'an run far deeper than you imagined.

zh: 你在暗巷的阴影中蹲守了半夜，终于等到了那个低语。一个裹着斗篷的身影匆匆走过，从怀中滑落了一封蜡封的信笺。借着月光匆匆一瞥——竟是{@npc_name}的把柄。你嘴角泛起一丝微笑，将信笺仔细收好，悄无声息地消失在了黑暗中。

en: You lurked in the shadows of the dark alley for half the night, and at last the whisper came. A cloaked figure hurried past, and from their sleeve slipped a wax-sealed letter. Under the moonlight, a furtive glance revealed — the leverage you needed on {@npc_name}. A faint smile crossed your lips. You tucked the letter away carefully and vanished into the darkness without a sound.

en: You respond with "{@lianju_picked_name}" as your image, earning {@lianju_score} renown![br]{@lianju_evaluation}
{@npc_couplet}[br][br]— A fine line, "{@lianju_npc_name}"! Now it's your turn to respond.

zh: 穿过重重院落，相府的奢华让你甚至不敢抬头。你被引至一处熏着沉香的幽静暖阁。珠帘掀开，那位权倾朝野的大唐右相，并没有端坐在高堂之上。
en: "I was merely teasing a fellow talent!"

zh: 是子美吗？快，上前些，让老夫好好看看。
en: You pass through courtyard after courtyard, the opulence of the Chancellor's manor so overwhelming you hardly dare lift your eyes. You are ushered into a quiet, warm chamber fragrant with aloeswood incense. The beaded curtain parts — and the man who holds the empire in his palm, the Grand Chancellor of the Great Tang, is not seated high upon a dais.

zh: 相爷，草民那卷《雕赋》……不知是否污了相爷的眼。
en: Is that Zimei? Come, come closer — let this old man have a proper look at you.

zh: （叹气）大唐太庞大了，朝堂上尽是些尸位素餐的蠢物。老夫昨夜挑灯将你的赋看了三遍……字字珠玑，这是王佐之才啊！
en: My Lord Chancellor, that scroll of mine, the "Rhapsody on the Eagle"... I only hope it did not offend Your Excellency's eyes.

zh: 他竟亲自离座，走到你面前。那双翻手为云覆手为雨的手，重重地、却又极具温度地拍了拍你的肩膀。
en: (sighs) The Great Tang is far too vast, and the court is stuffed with witless fools who merely occupy their posts. Last night I lit a lamp and read your rhapsody three times over... Every word a pearl, every phrase a gem — this is the talent of a king's counselor!

zh: 天下，太需要你这样的年轻人了。回去好好歇息，无需再四处奔波受气。明年的春闱科举，老夫要在紫宸殿的金榜上，看到你的名字
en: He actually rose from his seat and walked up to you. Those hands — hands that could overturn clouds into rain with a single turn — landed heavily, yet with startling warmth, upon your shoulders.

The realm desperately needs young men like you. Go home and rest well — no more trudging about, swallowing insults from petty men. When the spring imperial examinations come next year, this old man expects to see your name upon the golden roster in the Hall of Purple Dawn.

zh: 你终于获得了一次面见右相的机会

en: You have finally secured an audience with the Grand Chancellor

zh: 是时候去拜访一下那位一人之下的右相了...

en: The time has come to pay a visit to the Grand Chancellor — the man second only to the Emperor himself...

zh: 时运之风。势高则诸事顺遂，势低则举步维艰。每旬自然衰减，城府可稍加减缓。

en: The wind of fortune. When momentum is high, all endeavors flow smoothly; when low, every step is a struggle. Decays naturally each ten-day period; political cunning can slow the decline.
A faint stir of momentum — the path ahead begins to open
Fortune rising, all things falling into place
Momentum fully forged — nothing can stand in your way
The momentum of the realm converges upon me
Momentum shattered — obstacles at every turn
Unable to take a single step

zh: 铜钱银两，长安米贵。行卷、买酒、交游，样样要钱。无钱寸步难行。
en: The tide of history — all hearts turn as one

zh: 荷包微沉，多了几文铜钱
en: Copper cash and silver taels. Grain in Chang'an does not come cheap. Presenting scrolls, buying wine, social connections — everything demands coin. Without money, you cannot take a single step.
Your purse grows slightly heavier — a few more copper coins

zh: 你掂量着一大袋钱，沉重厚实
富可敌国！银钱堆积如山
en: You heft a heavy sack of coin — solid, weighty, substantial
Wealth to rival a kingdom! Silver and coin piled high as mountains
That one cost quite a bit
Ruined utterly, fortunes scattered to the wind...
The wealthiest for a hundred miles

zh: 这些轻薄的丝帛和宣纸，曾是你叩开长安权贵大门的敲门砖。你看着它们在火光中卷曲、发黑，变成一小撮灰烬。火很小，但足够让你的手指恢复一点知觉了。
en: Choose a manuscript and cast it into the fire

zh: 你的诗稿在火焰中化为灰烬。手指恢复了知觉。
en: These delicate sheets of silk and Xuan paper were once your keys to knock upon the gates of Chang'an's powerful. You watch them curl, blacken, and crumble into a small heap of ash in the firelight. The flame is small, but just enough to bring a hint of feeling back to your fingers.

zh: 你身上没有什么可烧的。但身体莫名回暖了一些。
en: Your manuscripts turn to ash in the flames. Feeling returns to your fingers.
You have nothing left on your person to burn. Yet somehow, a strange warmth spreads through your body.

zh: 你翻遍了全身，没有纸，没有酒，甚至连悲哀和愤怒的情绪都已被榨干。大唐已经没有什么东西可以让你拿来燃烧了。

en: You search every inch of your body — no paper, no wine, not even the emotions of grief and rage remain to be wrung out. The Great Tang has nothing left for you to set ablaze.

zh: 你舒展身体，回忆自己都做了什么...

en: You stretch your limbs and reflect on what you've been up to...

zh: 去马来牛不复辨，浊泾清渭何当分？
暴雨倾盆、道路泥泞，极目望去，连跑去的马和走来的牛都分不清了。连绵的阴雨让山洪暴发，原本清浊分明的泾河与渭河，此时又怎能分得清呢？
en: Horses depart, oxen arrive — who can tell them apart? The Jing runs muddy, the Wei runs clear — how could they ever be divided now?

Torrential rain pours, the roads a quagmire. Gazing out as far as the eye can see, even galloping horses and plodding oxen blur into indistinction. The endless downpour has stirred mountain floods — the Jing and Wei rivers, once so clearly divided between murk and clarity, how could anyone tell them apart now?

zh: 点击右下角理念按钮以决定何所往
莫再蹉跎于裘马清狂之间，立定志向当在今日——哪怕多历坎坷、走些弯路，也胜过在犹豫不决中白了少年头。
en: Click the Conviction button in the lower-right corner to decide your path forward

zh: 朝扣富儿门，暮随肥马尘。残杯与冷炙，到处潜悲辛。
en: No more wasting time in youthful frivolity — set your resolve today. Better to stumble and wander than to grow old in hesitation, your hair turning white before you ever began.

zh: 清晨去敲富豪的大门，傍晚随在达官贵人的马后吃尘土；吃的是别人的残羹冷炙，到处偷偷吞咽着悲伤与痛苦。即使如此的下贱，但仍然吃不上饭。
en: At dawn I knock on the rich man's gate; at dusk I follow fat horses' dust. Leftover wine and cold scraps — everywhere I swallow grief unseen.

zh: 朝扣富儿门，暮随肥马尘。残杯与冷炙，到处潜悲辛。
en: Knocking on wealthy doors at dawn, eating dust behind nobles' horses at dusk; surviving on others' leftovers, secretly swallowing sorrow and bitterness wherever you go. Even debasing yourself this way, you still can't get enough to eat.

zh: 清晨去敲富豪的大门，傍晚随在达官贵人的马后吃尘土；吃的是别人的残羹冷炙，到处偷偷吞咽着悲伤与痛苦。即使如此的下贱，但仍然吃不上饭。
en: At dawn I knock on the rich man's gate; at dusk I follow fat horses' dust. Leftover wine and cold scraps — everywhere I swallow grief unseen.

Knocking on wealthy doors at dawn, eating dust behind nobles' horses at dusk; surviving on others' leftovers, secretly swallowing sorrow and bitterness wherever you go. Even debasing yourself this way, you still can't get enough to eat.

zh: 去【坊市】行动出卖体力之后去【出游】可以有效获取生命。
昔年泰山清狂，不知薪米之贵；今入长安，方知出卖体力之迫切也。
en: After working at the [Market Ward] to sell your labor, going on an [Excursion] is an effective way to regain health.
In years past atop Mount Tai, carefree and wild, I never knew the cost of firewood and rice. Now entering Chang'an, I finally understand the urgency of selling one's labor.

zh: 去坊市出卖体力之后去出游可以有效获取额外的资源。
昔年泰山清狂，不知薪米之贵；今入长安，方知出卖体力之迫切也。
en: Working at the Market Ward to sell your labor, then going on an Excursion, is an effective way to gain extra resources.

zh: 疟疠三秋孰可忍，寒热百日相交战
en: In years past atop Mount Tai, carefree and wild, I never knew the cost of firewood and rice. Now entering Chang'an, I finally understand the urgency of selling one's labor.

zh: 体内的寒气与热毒像两支军队一样，在我的身体里交锋厮杀。
en: How can one endure three autumns of pestilence and plague? A hundred days of cold and fever clashing within.
Cold qi and heat toxin battle inside my body like two armies at war.

zh: …或许和西市地下神医打好关系到【相识】之后他有办法？
莫硬撑了！那寒热消渴非小疾，快去求医。莫等老来右臂偏枯、日夕枯渴，徒留一身病骨，悔之晚矣！
en: ...Perhaps the underground divine doctor of the West Market has a remedy once you've earned his [Acquaintance]?

Don't tough it out! That alternation of cold, fever, and wasting thirst is no minor ailment — go seek a doctor at once! Don't wait until old age, when your right arm withers and day and night you parch with thirst, leaving only a body of bone and sickness — by then it will be too late for regret!

zh: 你终于拿到了对应的官职，你唯一想做的事情就是回家报喜，改善家人的生活。

en: You've finally secured an official post. The only thing you want to do now is rush home with the good news and improve your family's life.
Leaving the City at Year's End
You decide to exchange a poem with {@target_npc}

zh:
同乡老张风尘仆仆地找到你，从怀里掏出一个灰布包裹塞进你手中。

「这是三十钱，乡里凑的。子美啊，你到长安也有些时日了，怎么还不去拜谒？这都第三旬了，再不去可就晚了！」

他说完，重重拍了拍你的肩，转身消失在街巷尽头。

（天意旁白：是时候了，点击右下角「拜谒」行动，叩响仕途的第一扇门。）
en: Accept the silver and thank the fellow villager

Your fellow villager Old Zhang finds you, travel-worn and dusty. He pulls a grey cloth bundle from his coat and presses it into your hands.

"Here's thirty coins, scraped together by the village. Zimei, you've been in Chang'an for some time now — why haven't you gone to pay your respects yet? It's already the third xun! Much longer and it'll be too late!"

He gives your shoulder a heavy pat, then turns and vanishes into the alley.

(Aside from Providence: The time has come. Tap the "Pay Respects" action in the lower right, and knock on the first door of officialdom.)

zh: 寒月孤雪落叶：羁旅登高，天地苍茫

en: Cold Moon, Lonely Snow, Falling Leaves: Climbing high on a distant journey, heaven and earth vast and boundless

zh: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首平平无奇的诗，自我安慰尚可，赠人则略显寒酸。

en: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This is a thoroughly unremarkable poem — passable for self-consolation, but rather shabby as a gift.

zh: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首颇有章法的诗，令人点头称赞，唯欠几分神来之笔。

en: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This poem has genuine craft — it earns nods of approval, lacking only that touch of divine inspiration.

zh: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首泣鬼惊神的绝唱！字字珠玑，力透纸背，必将千古流传。

en: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This is a masterpiece that moves ghosts and gods to tears! Each word a pearl, the brushwork biting through the page — this will be passed down through the ages.

zh: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。一首「{@poem_type}」诗已然落成。

en: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. A poem of "{@poem_type}" has taken form.

zh: 干将未省钝 + 主将收才子：献赋求荐，含蓄自尊
赠献纳使起居田舍人澄
en: Ganjiang unaware of his own dullness + the Commander gathers talents: offering verse to seek recommendation, restrained yet proud
For the Palace Provisioner, Drafter Tian of Qiju

zh: 求职诗的巅峰：骑驴十三载(羁旅) + 骅骝作骨(骐骥) + 致君尧舜上(尧舜)
奉赠韦左丞丈二十二韵
en: The pinnacle of job-seeking poetry: thirteen years on donkey-back (Wandering) + a steed's spirit in the bones (Noble Steed) + raising the sovereign to the level of Yao and Shun (Sages)

zh: 饥寒 + 明主：谏议底色，穷年忧黎
en: Twenty-Two Couplets Humbly Presented to Vice Director Wei
Hunger, Cold + A Wise Ruler: the remonstrator's essence — year after year of poverty, grieving for the common people
Ten Couplets Respectfully Presented to Remonstrator Zheng

zh: 才名与望誉。行卷投谒、风评交游的核心资本，是进入权贵圈层的入场券。

en: Reputation and renown. The core capital for submitting manuscripts, paying visits, and navigating social circles — your ticket into the world of the powerful.

zh: 才名渐起，坊间偶有传颂
en: Literary talent stirs; a faint name begins to rise.

zh: 声名鹊起，文人争相传颂
en: Your reputation grows; your name is occasionally praised in the streets.
Your fame soars; scholars compete to recite your works.
The literary star stirs; all under heaven knows your name.
Your literary name is slightly tarnished.
Your literary name is damaged, drawing considerable criticism.
Your name is in ruins; everyone spits at the mention of it.
A name that moves the world
Tossed on the sea of officialdom
A fledgling on the official path

zh: 袖口抹去坛沿的灰，仰头灌下第一口时，喉结还没动，鼻腔先涌出酸气。
更声敲到第三下时，你已经坐进东市那家不收欠据的酒肆。锣声在你决定不去数的今夜，敲得格外清楚——一共是五更，而你走了六条街才找到这家还亮着灯火的铺子。你在角落里坐下，手指按在桌面那道裂缝上，顺着它推过去，推回来。酒保把坛子往桌上一搁，没有看你。
袖口在墙灰上蹭出一道痕，铜钱已从腰间解下攥进手中
「三月十七·吏部东院·未时·携——」后面的字被雨水洇成淡青色的一团。纸边有撕扯时留下的毛刺。你站在墙前的时间长度，足够西边的云把日头吃掉一半。
指尖在筹身木纹的断茬处停了片刻，然后拿过来。
“上一个和你鞋底有一样泥的人，现在已不穿这双靴了。他拿了我一枚木筹，那天起，他的靴底再没沾过寺后泥土。”他从怀里摸出一枚拇指长的旧木筹，递到离你一尺远的地方，没有催促，只是让它悬在那里。
肩颈微微一僵。鞋尖转向床边，已迈了半步。
张垍旧宅偏院的槐树下，小厮引你到一处厢房。床上摊开一件半旧圆领袍，袖口磨得发亮，料子在暗处隐隐泛着青灰——不是新物，是被人穿过的。那人靠在门框上，没开口谈价。他说，上次穿着这件衣裳的人现在在万年县做县尉。又说，集贤院散席的时候，魏某人在门口看见这领子——唤了一声张公。说完他从袖中抽出一封信，是你三年前写给张垍的自荐诗。信纸在浆洗过的衣领旁展开，墨迹已经有些洇开了。他把信放在袍子上，什么也没说。
杜甫端碗饮尽，也不道谢，只说：正好练笔。碗底叩在桌上的声响干脆利落。
杜甫看着晃动的酒碗，手指在桌沿停了一瞬，才说：知道了。
杜甫点头记下，随后问起王员外的交游——他最近跟谁走得近？
