漁陽鼙鼓動地來，驚破霓裳羽衣曲。你在戰火中歸鄉，卻發現家園已成廢墟，而自己也未能躲過這場浩劫……

en: Gazing into the distance, the peak remains shrouded in that thick bank of fog. Who knows when you'll finally behold Mount Tai's true face.
"Go on." He waves a hand, his expression serene. "You and I share a bond of affinity. We shall meet again, in time."

You bow deeply, turn, and set out on the road home. After a few steps, you cannot help but glance back — the Taoist has already turned toward the mountain, his figure slowly vanishing into the forest.
This journey to Mount Tai has profited you greatly, you think. You will return to pay a visit someday.
What you do not realize is that this parting will stretch across twenty years.

The clouds beneath your feet churn like an ocean of waves. Distant peaks emerge and vanish in the sea of mist, like azure islands floating in a white expanse. The dome of heaven arches above, the stars arrayed across it, and for a moment you feel utterly alone between sky and earth.
Ten thousand leagues of deep-blue waves surge and roll — the sun and moon seem to rise from within them, the River of Stars to pour from their depths.

zh: 高原上的雄狮，时刻觊觎着河西走廊与安西四镇。
en: Scroll after scroll of bamboo slips unfurl before your eyes, filled with the names of those who rose and fell, who triumphed and perished.
You suddenly understand — this magnificent landscape, this is the poetry you are meant to write.
He slowly opens his eyes, studies you for a moment, then speaks: "Young man, why have you come to Mount Tai?"

zh: 前往泰山东麓，寻找幽静的山谷
en: The mountain wind rises, and the fog churns like a tide. For a moment you think you glimpse the silhouette of the summit — then it is gone, as if it were never there.
You think of the Taoist — he has cultivated on this mountain for many years. Perhaps he knows the origin of this fog.
You rack your brains for what feels like an eternity, but all you manage are a few dry, lifeless lines. Even you shake your head at them.

zh:
你在泰山山间漫步，呼吸着新鲜空气。山风吹过，树叶沙沙作响，偶尔几声鸟鸣从远处传来。

远远望去，山顶仍被那团浓雾笼罩着。不知何时才能一睹泰山真容。
en: You recall the Taoist's words — "Mountaineering is not won with the brush." Perhaps you still need something more.
The Taoist, you realize, has been standing behind you for some time. He leans over to glance at the draft, and a flash of astonishment crosses his eyes.

zh: 云雾散尽，抬头仰望泰山之巅
en: "Fine! Fine indeed! 'I must ascend the utmost peak, and see all other mountains dwarfed beneath!'" The Taoist claps his hands in praise. "Young man, with a poetic gift like this, you will surely win great renown. A name inscribed in the annals of history is no idle dream."
"You're back." His tone is calm. "Judging by your expression — what did you encounter?"

You stand at the cliff's edge, looking down at the mountain ranges stretching to the edge of the sky. An indescribable emotion swells in your chest. The world is so vast — and you are but a speck of dust within it.

zh: 攀上北面岩壁，远眺泰山主峰
en: The Taoist comes to stand beside you and speaks softly: "This humble priest must sit in meditation for a while. Go wander where you will. These mountains still hold much worth seeing."
With that, he finds a green stone, settles cross-legged upon it, closes his eyes, and speaks no more.

zh: 沿着山间溪流向南，寻幽访胜
en: Gazing into the distance, the peak remains shrouded in that thick bank of fog. Who knows when you'll finally behold Mount Tai's true face.
"Go on." He waves a hand, his expression serene. "You and I share a bond of affinity. We shall meet again, in time."

zh: 登上西边山岭，观赏云海奇景
en: You bow deeply, turn, and set out on the road home. After a few steps, you cannot help but glance back — the Taoist has already turned toward the mountain, his figure slowly vanishing into the forest.
This journey to Mount Tai has profited you greatly, you think. You will return to pay a visit someday.
What you do not realize is that this parting will stretch across twenty years.

zh:
两旬时光匆匆而过。这一日清晨，你来到道士打坐处，见他缓缓睁开眼睛。

「成了。」道士拂尘一挥。

你抬头望去，笼罩山顶的浓雾正以肉眼可见的速度消散。阳光穿透云层，将泰山之巅染成一片金黄。那巍峨的山体第一次完整地展现在你面前——这就是泰山，如画，如诗。
en: The clouds beneath your feet churn like an ocean of waves. Distant peaks emerge and vanish in the sea of mist, like azure islands floating in a white expanse. The dome of heaven arches above, the stars arrayed across it, and for a moment you feel utterly alone between sky and earth.
Ten thousand leagues of deep-blue waves surge and roll — the sun and moon seem to rise from within them, the River of Stars to pour from their depths.
Scroll after scroll of bamboo slips unfurl before your eyes, filled with the names of those who rose and fell, who triumphed and perished.

zh:
你贸然打断了道士的作法。他手中拂尘一顿，周身气息散了开去。

道士转过头，眉头紧皱：「年轻人，作法讲究一气呵成，你这一打断，贫道又得重头来过。」

他叹了口气，重新闭上双眼：「罢了罢了，下不为例。」
en: You suddenly understand — this magnificent landscape, this is the poetry you are meant to write.
He slowly opens his eyes, studies you for a moment, then speaks: "Young man, why have you come to Mount Tai?"

zh: 等待道士行动。如果打断他可能不会很开心。
en: The mountain wind rises, and the fog churns like a tide. For a moment you think you glimpse the silhouette of the summit — then it is gone, as if it were never there.
You think of the Taoist — he has cultivated on this mountain for many years. Perhaps he knows the origin of this fog.
You rack your brains for what feels like an eternity, but all you manage are a few dry, lifeless lines. Even you shake your head at them.

zh: 在下杜甫，此番游历是为增长见识
en: 远远望去，山顶仍被那团浓雾笼罩着。不知何时才能一睹泰山真容。

zh: 道士打量了你一番，笑道：「贫道在此山修行多年，看人倒也有几分眼力。小友脚步稳健，不像寻常书生那般弱不禁风。」\n\n他拂尘轻摆，示意你坐下：「未请教大名？此番来泰山，所为何事？」
en: You wander through Mount Tai's slopes, breathing the crisp mountain air. The wind rustles through the leaves, and birdsong drifts from afar.\n\nGazing into the distance, the summit remains shrouded in that thick bank of fog. Who knows when you will finally behold Mount Tai's true face.
The Taoist, you realize, has been standing behind you for some time. He leans over to glance at the draft, and a flash of astonishment crosses his eyes.

"Fine! Fine indeed! 'I must ascend the utmost peak, and see all other mountains dwarfed beneath!'" The Taoist claps his hands in praise. "Young man, with a poetic gift like this, you will surely win great renown. A name inscribed in the annals of history is no idle dream."

zh:
道士闻言，微微颔首：「年纪轻轻便有此志，难得。」

他伸手在你肩上按了按，又看了看你的脸色：「身子骨还算硬朗，面色也红润——看来家中不曾亏待了你。出门在外，身体是本钱，钱财是盘缠。这两样本钱，你得时时放在心上。」

他从袖中取出一枚铜钱把玩：「贫道云游四方，深知一文钱难倒英雄汉。好在你眼下囊中尚不羞涩，趁年轻多走走。」
en: "You're back." His tone is calm. "Judging by your expression — what did you encounter?"

You stand at the cliff's edge, looking down at the mountain ranges stretching to the edge of the sky. An indescribable emotion swells in your chest. The world is so vast — and you are but a speck of dust within it.
The Taoist comes to stand beside you and speaks softly: "This humble priest must sit in meditation for a while. Go wander where you will. These mountains still hold much worth seeing."

zh:
道士将铜钱递还给你，正色道：「杜小友，贫道观你不是甘于庸碌之人。你这等读书人，心里都揣着一团火——那是志向，是抱负。」

他抬手指向远方：「你且看这天地。有人为名利奔波，有人为家国忧心。读圣贤书，所为者何？」

他顿了顿：「文思、声望、时运——这三样东西，日后会推着你往前走，也会在关键时刻绊你一脚。心中有数，方能行远。」
en: With that, he finds a green stone, settles cross-legged upon it, closes his eyes, and speaks no more.
Follow the mountain stream southward, seeking out secluded beauty.

zh:
道士又看了你几眼，忽然说道：「我观你才思尚可，但身子骨还需磨砺。登山不是靠笔杆子，是靠腿脚。你这副身板，若不先打熬打熬，怕是走不了多远。」

他站起身，拍了拍道袍上的尘土，在你肩上按了按，力道不轻不重。

「嗯，底子不错。我见过不少读书人，十年寒窗下来不是弯腰就是驼背。你这副筋骨，比他们强。」

他简单教了你几式调息之法，嘱咐道：「登山之人，气力是本钱。记着这个道理。」

en: Ascend the western ridge and behold the wondrous sea of clouds.

zh: 晚辈生于大唐开元十五年，今年该是二十有六了
en: The fog has lifted! Look — Mount Tai!

zh:
道士捻须一笑：「贫道久居山中，对年月已不甚在意。小友可知今夕是何年？」

他望向远处天际，目光似乎穿透了云层：「修道之人不计春秋，但你这读书人，须得心中有数。何时赶考、何时进京，都是要紧事。」

他伸手指向山外：「记着时日，莫负光阴。」

en:
Two tendays pass in the blink of an eye. One morning, you arrive at the Taoist's meditation spot and find him slowly opening his eyes.

"It is done." The Taoist sweeps his horsetail whisk.

You look up. The dense fog shrouding the summit is dissipating before your very eyes. Sunlight pierces the clouds, dyeing Mount Tai's peak a brilliant gold. For the first time, the majestic mountain reveals itself in full before you — this is Mount Tai, a painting, a poem.

zh:
你取出随身携带的酒囊，在道士面前晃了晃。

道士眼睛一亮：「好小子，来泰山还带着酒？」

你们二人在青石上对坐，几杯下肚，道士的话匣子渐渐打开。他讲起年轻时云游各处的见闻，讲起各处的风土人情，语气中透着几分过来人的感慨。

酒酣耳热，你感觉与这道士之间的距离近了不少。
en:
You rashly interrupt the Taoist's ritual. His whisk freezes mid-motion, and the gathered aura scatters around him.

The Taoist turns his head, brow furrowed deep: "Young man, ritual workings must flow in one unbroken breath. With this disruption, this humble priest must begin anew from the very start."

He sighs and closes his eyes once more: "Enough, enough. Let it not happen again."
Wait for the Taoist to act. Interrupting him may not go over well.

zh:
你站在山巅，回望这一路——从山脚遇道士，到山腰得指点，再到此刻俯瞰万山。

风从四面八方吹来，你忽然感觉自己不再只是那个初出茅庐的书生了。泰山的灵秀之气仿佛渗入了你的骨血，那些不曾想过的才华、那些深藏的城府、那份与生俱来的定力，都在这一刻变得清晰起来。

再看这天地，你有了新的感悟——朝堂的风声、人间的恩怨、那些暗流涌动的关系网，都隐隐浮现。

泰山之行，不虚此行。

[size=13][color=#888888]系统提示：新的界面元素已解锁。右下角的按钮可查看人脉、理念、诗词等功能[/color][/size]
en: He sits down and begins the ritual.
I am Du Fu. I travel to broaden my knowledge of the world.

zh:
离别的日子终于到了。你在山脚下与玄明道人告别。

「去吧。」道士挥了挥手，神色平静，「你我有缘，日后自会再见。」

你深深鞠了一躬，转身踏上归途。走出几步，又忍不住回头看了一眼——道士已转身走向山中，身形渐渐隐入林间。

你心想，此番泰山之行使你获益良多，日后再来拜访。

只是你没想到，这一别，竟过了二十年。
en: The Taoist sizes you up, then smiles: \"This humble priest has cultivated on this mountain for many years and has learned to read a man. Your steps are steady, young friend — not frail like the typical scholar.\"\n\nHe gestures with his whisk, beckoning you to sit: \"May I ask your distinguished name? What brings you to Mount Tai?\"
A Chance Meeting in the Mountains

zh:
站在泰山之巅，你俯瞰着脚下的云海和远方的山河。此行泰山的收获远超预期。

你心中隐隐有了些关于未来的想法——虽然还很模糊，但你能感觉到，自己的人生不该只是随波逐流。

点击右下角蓝色印章，将这份感悟化为前行的方向。
en:
The Taoist nods slightly: "To possess such ambition at your age — rare indeed."

He presses a hand on your shoulder and studies your complexion: "Your frame is sturdy, your color healthy — your family has not neglected you. When abroad in the world, your body is your capital and coin is your provision. Keep both ever in mind."

He produces a copper coin from his sleeve and toys with it: "This humble priest has wandered far and wide. I know well how a single copper coin can humble even the mightiest of men. Your purse is not yet empty — travel while you are young."

zh:
你站在山巅，迎着猎猎山风，心中涌起一股从未有过的豪情。

道士的话又在耳边响起——「人生在世，最要紧的是什么？」

那时你没有回答。但现在，你心中有了答案。天下这么大，总有一条路，是为你准备的。
en:
The Taoist returns the coin to you, his tone turning earnest: "Young Du, this humble priest sees that you are not one content with mediocrity. Scholars like you carry a fire within their hearts — that is ambition, that is purpose."

He raises a hand toward the distance: "Look upon this world. Some chase fame and fortune. Some worry for family and country. You study the sages — to what end, then?"

He pauses: "Literary genius, renown, fortune's favor — these three will propel you forward, yet they will trip you at critical moments. Know their measure, and you shall travel far."
Thank you for your guidance, Master.

The Taoist gives you another long look, then speaks: "Your literary talent is passable, but your body still needs tempering. Mountaineering is not won with the brush — it is won with the legs. This frame of yours — if you do not first weather it, I fear you will not travel far."

He rises, dusts off his robe, and presses a hand on your shoulder — not too light, not too heavy.

"Mm. Your foundation is solid. I have seen many scholars — after ten years buried in books, they emerge stooped and hunched. Your frame is stronger than theirs."

He teaches you a few breathing exercises and counsels: "One who climbs mountains — vigor is your capital. Remember this truth."

This junior was born in the fifteenth year of the Kaiyuan era of the Great Tang. I should be twenty-six this year.

The Taoist strokes his beard and laughs: "This humble priest has dwelt long in the mountains — the passing of months and years has grown faint to me. But tell me, young friend — do you know what year it is now?"

He gazes toward the distant horizon, his eyes seeming to pierce the clouds: "One who cultivates the Way counts not the seasons, but a scholar like you must keep them in mind. When to sit the examinations, when to enter the capital — these are matters of consequence."

He points beyond the mountains: "Mark the days. Do not squander time."

zh:
你登上泰山之巅，极目远眺。

脚下的云雾如海浪般翻涌，远处群山在云海中若隐若现，如同浮在白色汪洋中的青色岛屿。天穹如盖，星斗罗列其间，天地间仿佛只剩下你一人。

万里沧波翻涌，日月若出其中，星汉灿烂若出其里。

一页页竹简在眼前展开，上面写满了兴亡成败的名字。

你忽然明白——这壮丽山河，便是你要书写的诗行。

en: Share a drink with the Taoist Master.

zh: 我来游历天下，增长见识
en:
You produce the wineskin from your belt and wave it before the Taoist.

The Taoist's eyes light up: "Well done, lad! You brought wine to Mount Tai?"

The two of you sit facing each other on the green stone. After a few cups, the Taoist's reserve loosens. He recounts tales from his wandering youth — the customs and peoples of distant lands — his voice tinged with a veteran's nostalgia.

Warm with wine, you feel the distance between you and this Taoist shrink considerably.

zh: 我……我也不知道，就是觉得该来

泰山巍峨，山脚下鸟语花香，溪水潺潺。你正沉醉于这天地间的灵气，忽见一位白发道士端坐于青石之上。他仙风道骨，手持拂尘，双目微阖，像是早已在此等候多时。

他缓缓睁开眼，打量着你片刻，开口问道：「少年人，你为何来到这泰山？」
en:
You stand at the summit and look back upon the road you have traveled — from meeting the Taoist at the mountain's foot, to receiving his guidance on the slopes, to this moment gazing down upon ten thousand peaks.

The wind rushes in from every direction, and you suddenly feel you are no longer just that callow young scholar. Mount Tai's numinous spirit seems to have seeped into your very blood. Talents you never imagined, depths of shrewdness long hidden, a composure born within you — all become sharp and clear in this moment.

You look upon the world anew with fresh insight — the whispers of the court, the grudges and debts among men, the undercurrents of power and connection — all loom before you, faint but unmistakable.

This journey to Mount Tai has not been in vain.

zh:
你沿着山路走到了泰山另一侧。抬头想看清山顶的轮廓，却发现一层浓雾将山头裹得严严实实，什么也看不见。

山风一起，雾气翻涌如浪，隐约间似乎能瞧见山巅的轮廓，又好像什么都没有。

你想起了道士——他在此山修行多年，或许知道这雾的来历。
en: 「去吧。」道士挥了挥手，神色平静，「你我有缘，日后自会再见。」
你深深鞠了一躬，转身踏上归途。走出几步，又忍不住回头看了一眼——道士已转身走向山中，身形渐渐隐入林间。
你心想，此番泰山之行使你获益良多，日后再来拜访。
只是你没想到，这一别，竟过了二十年。

zh:
你面对壮丽的山河，想要写一首诗记录下来。然而提起笔，脑中却一片空白。

搜肠刮肚半天，只写出几句干巴巴的字句，连你自己看了都摇头。

你想起道士说过的话——「登山不是靠笔杆子」。或许，你还需要一点别的什么。
en:
The day of parting arrives at last. At the foot of the mountain, you bid farewell to Taoist Master Xuanming.

"Go on." He waves a hand, his expression serene. "You and I share a bond of affinity. We shall meet again, in time."

You bow deeply, turn, and set out on the road home. After a few steps, you cannot help but glance back — the Taoist has already turned toward the mountain, his figure slowly vanishing into the forest.

This journey to Mount Tai has profited you greatly, you think. You will return to pay a visit someday.

What you do not realize is that this parting will stretch across twenty years.
A direction seems to have formed in my heart.

zh:
几杯药酒下肚，文思果然如泉涌。你一气呵成写下一首《望岳》，字里行间尽是少年人的锐气与壮志。

道士不知何时已站在你身后，探头看了一眼诗稿，眼中闪过惊艳之色。

「好！好一句『会当凌绝顶，一览众山小』！」道士拍手称赞，「年轻人，你这诗才，他日必有大名，青史留名不在话下。」
en:
Standing atop Mount Tai, you look down upon the sea of clouds at your feet and the mountains and rivers stretching into the distance. This journey has yielded far more than you expected.

Vague thoughts about the future stir within you — still indistinct, but you can feel that your life should be more than drifting with the current.

Click the blue stamp in the lower-right corner to crystallize this insight into a direction forward.

zh: 你在泰山脚下寻了一处青石坐下。山风轻拂，草木清香扑鼻。远处传来几声鸟鸣，更显得山间幽静。歇息片刻，你决定继续前行。
en:
You stand at the summit, the fierce mountain wind whipping past you, and a heroic fervor like never before surges within your chest.

The Taoist's words echo in your ears — "What matters most in this life?"

You had no answer then. But now, the answer rests in your heart. The world is vast — somewhere, a path awaits that is meant for you.

zh: 山腰处的风景与山脚迥然不同。松涛阵阵，云雾时聚时散。你靠在树干上，望着远处的层峦叠嶂，心中涌起一股登高望远的豪情。

en: Exchange a few words with the Taoist Master.

zh: 山顶被大雾罩着，什么也看不见

你回到道士打坐的青石旁。他仍是那副云淡风轻的模样，但听到脚步声便已睁开眼。

「回来了。」他语气平静，「看你的表情，是遇到了什么？」

en: 脚下的云雾如海浪般翻涌，远处群山在云海中若隐若现，如同浮在白色汪洋中的青色岛屿。天穹如盖，星斗罗列其间，天地间仿佛只剩下你一人。
万里沧波翻涌，日月若出其中，星汉灿烂若出其里。

zh:
你走近道士打坐的青石旁，轻声唤了几句。「道长？」

道士盘膝而坐，双目紧闭，呼吸悠长，似乎已入定境。你等了片刻，他依然没有任何回应。

看来道长正在修炼的关键时刻，不便打扰。还是先去别处转转吧。
en: 一页页竹简在眼前展开，上面写满了兴亡成败的名字。
你忽然明白——这壮丽山河，便是你要书写的诗行。

You scale Mount Tai's summit and gaze into the far distance.

The clouds beneath your feet churn like an ocean of waves. Distant peaks emerge and vanish in the sea of mist, like azure islands floating in a white expanse. The dome of heaven arches above, the stars arrayed across it, and for a moment you feel utterly alone between sky and earth.

Ten thousand leagues of deep-blue waves surge and roll — the sun and moon seem to rise from within them, the River of Stars to pour from their depths.

Scroll after scroll of bamboo slips unfurl before your eyes, filled with the names of those who rose and fell, who triumphed and perished.

You suddenly understand — this magnificent landscape, this is the poetry you are meant to write.

zh:
道士在你肩上拍了拍，力道不轻不重。

「嗯，底子不错。我见过不少读书人，十年寒窗下来不是弯腰就是驼背。你这副筋骨，比他们强。」

他简单教了你几式调息之法，嘱咐道：「登山之人，气力是本钱。记着这个道理。」
en: I travel the realm to broaden my understanding.
I have come seeking inspiration for my poetry.
I... I don't know either. I just felt I had to come.

zh:
道士带你绕过几条山路，眼前豁然开朗——一整片开阔的山谷，远处群山如黛，云海翻涌。风声穿过松林，带着湿润的草木气息。

你站在崖边，看着脚下绵延至天际的山脉，胸中涌起一股说不清的情绪。天地如此之大，而你只是其中一粒尘埃。

道士在你身旁站定，轻声道：「贫道需打坐片刻，你自去转转吧。这山间还有不少可看之处。」

说罢，他寻了一块青石盘膝坐下，闭上双眼，不再言语。
en: 他缓缓睁开眼，打量着你片刻，开口问道：「少年人，你为何来到这泰山？」

Mount Tai stands majestic. At its foot, birds sing among fragrant blossoms, and brooks murmur over smooth stones. You are drinking in the numinous spirit of this place when you suddenly notice a white-haired Taoist seated upon a green boulder. His bearing is transcendent, a horsetail whisk in hand, his eyes gently closed — as though he has been waiting here for you all along.\n\nHe slowly opens his eyes, studies you for a moment, then speaks: \"Young man, why have you come to Mount Tai?\"
At the Foot of Mount Tai
山风一起，雾气翻涌如浪，隐约间似乎能瞧见山巅的轮廓，又好像什么都没有。
你想起了道士——他在此山修行多年，或许知道这雾的来历。

zh: 你去找了几个朋友运作了一下
en:
You follow the mountain path to the other side of Mount Tai. You look up, hoping to make out the summit's outline — only to find a dense fog wrapped tight around the peak, revealing nothing.

The mountain wind rises, and the fog churns like a tide. For a moment you think you glimpse the silhouette of the summit — then it is gone, as if it were never there.

You think of the Taoist — he has cultivated on this mountain for many years. Perhaps he knows the origin of this fog.

zh: 你提笔悬腕，却迟迟落不下去——这诗稿上的批注字字如刀，你无从下笔。清客见状，微微摇头，将诗稿收回袖中。
en: Seems I'll need some wine to stir the muse.

zh: 将袖中所有银钱尽数倒在他摊开的掌中

en: 搜肠刮肚半天，只写出几句干巴巴的字句，连你自己看了都摇头。

zh: 将剩余银钱尽数倒出，期望他可以放了你
en: 你想起道士说过的话——「登山不是靠笔杆子」。或许，你还需要一点别的什么。

zh: 相府青鞜大门半开，门房的胖汉横跨在石阶上，正用小指抠着牙缝，连正眼都没落在一个穿布衣的访客身上。当你踏上第一级台阶，一截包着铜皮的水火棍猛地横扫过来，险些砸碎你的膝盖。「相爷府的门，也配沾你的酸泥？」胖汉冷哼一声，蒲扇般的手掌直直摊在你眼前。他掂了掂另一只手里的空钱袋，铜钱碰撞的暗哑声在寒风里格外刺耳。
en:
You face the magnificent landscape, brush in hand, determined to capture it in verse. Yet as you raise the brush, your mind goes blank.

You rack your brains for what feels like an eternity, but all you manage are a few dry, lifeless lines. Even you shake your head at them.

You recall the Taoist's words — "Mountaineering is not won with the brush." Perhaps you still need something more.

zh: 门卫对你虎视眈眈，不交钱还想走？
en: The Well of Words Runs Dry
Ask the Master for his critique.
道士不知何时已站在你身后，探头看了一眼诗稿，眼中闪过惊艳之色。

zh: 再次来到相府门前。那胖大门房正与一个西域商贾低声调笑，余光扫到你走近。他甚至没有停下嘴里的诨话，只是懒洋洋地用鞋底踢开挡在路中间的扫帚，留出一条仅供一人侧身挤入的缝隙，随后便低下头，继续盘算着手里新得的银锞子。你掸去袖上的灰尘，从那道狭窄的缝隙中艰难挤入。
en: 「好！好一句『会当凌绝顶，一览众山小』！」道士拍手称赞，「年轻人，你这诗才，他日必有大名，青史留名不在话下。」

After a few cups of medicinal wine, inspiration indeed flows like a spring. You dash off "Gazing on Mount Tai" in a single breath — every line brimming with a young man's edge and soaring ambition.

The Taoist, you realize, has been standing behind you for some time. He leans over to glance at the draft, and a flash of astonishment crosses his eyes.

"Fine! Fine indeed! 'I must ascend the utmost peak, and see all other mountains dwarfed beneath!'" The Taoist claps his hands in praise. "Young man, with a poetic gift like this, you will surely win great renown. A name inscribed in the annals of history is no idle dream."

zh: 上前一步，拱手请命：在下愿献拙作
将身上余钱塞给清客，低声求通融
穿过前院，堂下站着一位着青袍的掌书记。他正用一柄玉如意逗弄着廊下的画眉，听闻你自报家门，他停下手中的玉如意，目光终于落在你破旧的衣摆上。「子美？听说你在洛阳薄有诗名。」他端起茶盏，杯盖轻轻撇去浮沫，发出清脆的刮擦声，「相爷今日乏了。若没有能镇得住这满堂锦绣的千古绝唱，就别拿那些俗物来污了右相府的青砖。」
en: You find a green boulder at the foot of Mount Tai and sit. The mountain breeze brushes past, carrying the clean scent of grass and trees. Birdsong drifts from afar, deepening the mountain stillness. After a short rest, you decide to press onward.

The scenery at mid-mountain is wholly different from the foot. Pine winds roar in waves, and the mist gathers and scatters by turns. You lean against a tree trunk, gazing at the layered ridges receding into the distance. A bold yearning to climb higher and see farther surges within you.

zh: 你再次步入前堂。那青袍掌书记正低头翻阅着你昨日呕心沥血献上的诗卷，甚至随手拿朱笔在上面乱勾了几笔。你急忙上前一步拱手，他却仿佛没看见面前这个大活人似的，径直向一旁的侍女招手：「这诗稿的纸张质地太糙，拿去垫偏殿那张缺了角的酸枝木桌吧，莫要划伤了相爷的玉管笔。」从头到尾，他的目光未曾在你身上停留半寸。

en: The summit is blanketed in thick fog — nothing can be seen.

You return to the green boulder where the Taoist meditates. He remains as serene as drifting clouds, yet the moment he hears your footsteps, his eyes open.\n\n\"You're back.\" His tone is calm. \"Judging by your expression — what did you encounter?\"

zh: 拐过街角，一面高耸得仿佛没有尽头的青砖坊墙将天光生生截断。几十个穿着旧青袍或麻布衣的士子，像冻僵的鹌鹑一样贴着墙根瑟缩排开，没人敢出声，连咳嗽都被死死捂在袖子里。你走到队伍最末端站定。抬头望去，三丈高的朱漆大门紧紧闭合，两尊巨大的石狮子在阴影中俯视着阶下的蝼蚁。一阵穿堂冷风卷过，门上磨盘大小的兽面衔环发出一声沉闷的金属撞击音，墙根下的几十颗脑袋同时条件反射般地瑟缩了一下。你呼出的白气，在这堵绝对寂静的高墙前，瞬间便被吹得粉碎。

en: Round the corner, and a soaring blue-brick compound wall—seemingly without end—shears the daylight in two. Dozens of scholars in faded green robes or coarse hemp garments huddle against the wall's base like frozen quails, shoulder to shoulder, none daring to make a sound; even coughs are smothered dead in their sleeves. You walk to the very end of the line and stop. Looking up, the three-zhang vermilion gates are shut tight. Two colossal stone lions glower down from the shadows at the ants beneath the steps. A draft of cold corridor wind sweeps through, and the millstone-sized beast-head knocker on the gate lets out a dull metallic clang. Dozens of heads along the wall base flinch in unison, a reflexive shudder. The white mist of your breath, before this wall of absolute silence, is instantly blown to nothing.

zh: 长安平康坊以南，右相府邸的坊墙连绵如铁。你沿街疾走，晨霜早已湿透了麻鞋。越靠近那两扇高耸的朱漆大门，周围的喧闹声便越是被一种死寂的威压吞没。你的手死死攥着袖口中那卷拜帖，骨节因过度用力而惨白。抬起头，相府门楼上的琉璃兽脊仿佛要刺破厚重的云层，你死死盯着那高不可攀的门槛，喉结艰难地滚动了一下，连呼吸都忘了吐出。

en: South of Pingkang Ward in Chang'an, the Right Chancellor's compound wall stretches unbroken like iron. You hurry along the street, morning frost long since soaking through your hemp shoes. The closer you draw to those towering vermilion gates, the more the surrounding clamor is swallowed by a deathly, oppressive silence. Your hand clutches the visiting card inside your sleeve, knuckles bone-white from the grip. Looking up, the glazed beast-ridge tiles atop the mansion gate tower seem ready to pierce the thick cloud layer. You stare fixedly at that unreachable threshold, your Adam's apple bobbing with difficulty, forgetting even to exhale.

zh: 向郑虔展示诗作换取灵感与文名
en: On the Road to the Chancellor's Mansion

zh: 郑虔见你登门，欣然与你论诗谈文。你将从平康坊郑虔处所得的感悟融入诗稿，文思略有进益。
en: Show Zheng Qian your poems in exchange for inspiration and literary renown.

Zheng Qian sees you at his door and gladly discusses poetry and prose with you. You incorporate the insights gained from Zheng Qian at Pingkang Ward into your drafts; your literary thoughts show modest progress.
Zheng Qian · Trading Poems for Inspiration and Fame
Zheng Qian · Trading Poems for Inspiration and Fame

zh: 掷杯在地，拂袖间掀翻案上酒盏。
堆出笑容，双手捧起酒壶为对方斟满。
en: Hurl the cup to the floor, sweeping your sleeve to overturn the wine vessels on the table.

zh: 沉默片刻，问他那位同僚手里有什么可以交换。
en: Put on a smile, lift the wine flask with both hands, and fill the other's cup to the brim.

zh: “子美兄，我有个同僚想见户部的人。价钱好说。”说这话时他的眼睛没看你，看的是你身后那扇门——门后是今日宴席上所有正在交易的秘密。他笃定你还在这张桌上。
en: Fall silent for a moment, then ask what his colleague has to offer in exchange.

"Zimei, my friend, a colleague of mine needs to meet someone at the Ministry of Revenue. The price is negotiable." As he speaks, his eyes are not on you but on the door behind you—the door behind which all the day's dealings at this banquet are being transacted in secret. He is certain you are still seated at this table.

zh: 转身抬脚就走，名帖在身后落地。
双袖一振顺势跪下，额头已触到石阶。
en: Turn and stride away, the visiting card falling to the ground behind you.

zh: 从袖中摸出一张折好的纸，推过桌面。
en: With a shake of both sleeves, drop to your knees in one motion, forehead already touching the stone steps.

zh: “上次你递的干谒诗，老爷压在案角看了三日。这次又来了？”他往前凑了半步，嗓音压到只有檐下能听见：“不过老爷听说，赵主事那条盐铁司的路子，是你给牵的线。你要是有什么消息或是条件，我一并进去说。”廊柱的影子斜在两人之间，他在等一个数字。
en: Draw a folded slip of paper from your sleeve and slide it across the table.

"The last poem of self-recommendation you submitted—the Master kept it on the corner of his desk for three days. Now you've come again?" He leans half a step closer, his voice dropping to where only the eaves can hear: "Though the Master has heard that the salt-and-iron monopoly route through Secretary Zhao—you were the one who brokered it. If you have any news or terms, I'll convey them together when I go in." The shadow of the corridor pillar slants between the two of you. He is waiting for a number.

zh: 名帖往地上一掷，转身踩着新靴踏出廊去。
腰一弯，笑容堆满脸，双手将名帖捧过头顶。
en: Fling the visiting card to the floor, turn, and stride out of the corridor in new boots.

zh: 掂了掂袖中另一条消息，走向厅侧等他的管事。
en: Bend at the waist, pile a smile onto your face, and raise the visiting card above your head with both hands.

zh: “客人又来了。”他说完就走了，托盘在肘边晃了一下，映出灯影——那块漆掉了一块，露出旧木，上次你见它时还没掉。
en: Weigh the other piece of intelligence in your sleeve, then walk toward the steward waiting at the side of the hall.

"The guest is here again." He says this and leaves, the tray swaying at his elbow, catching the lamplight—a patch of lacquer has chipped off, revealing old wood beneath. The last time you saw it, the chip wasn't there.

zh: 拂袖打翻那杯酒，杯盏在案上滚出刺耳的声响。
双手接过酒杯一口饮尽，堆着笑连声应承。
en: Sweep your sleeve and knock over that cup of wine; the vessel rolls across the table with a grating sound.

zh: 用食指抵住杯沿慢慢推回半寸，报出一个诗题和价码。
en: Take the cup with both hands, drain it in one gulp, and assent repeatedly with a smile piled high.

zh: 贡院东墙外的小酒馆，灯笼在秋风中晃。几个举子的议论声从角落飘来——「那首《登科后》真是意气风发」「听说是张侍郎公子的手笔」。你认得那首诗。三个月前在张府后院，你用了两壶酒的时间把那些句子排好，换来一纸谒帖的承诺。现在张公子端着酒杯走过来了，靴底踩在松木地板上，每一步都稳得很。「子美兄，我爹很满意上回那首。这次再来一首？」酒杯往你这边推了半寸，杯沿上的唇印还没干透。他的语气像在谈一笔已经成交的买卖。
en: Press your index finger against the cup's rim and slowly push it back half an inch, naming a poem title and a price.

The small tavern outside the eastern wall of the examination hall, its lantern swaying in the autumn wind. Snatches of conversation drift from a corner where several examination candidates sit—"That poem 'After Passing the Exam' is truly spirited"—"I heard it was the handiwork of Vice Minister Zhang's son." You recognize that poem. Three months ago, in the rear courtyard of the Zhang residence, you spent two pots of wine arranging those lines in exchange for a promise of a recommendation letter. Now young Master Zhang is walking over, cup in hand, his boot soles steady on the pine floorboards, each step assured. "Zimei, my father was most satisfied with the last one. How about another?" The wine cup is nudged half an inch toward you, the lip print on its rim still wet. His tone is that of someone discussing a transaction already closed.

zh: 拂袖将茶碗扫落，纸条在湿痕里裂成两半。
双手接过那张报价单，脸上堆出笑容，腰已弯下三分。
en: Sweep your sleeve and knock the tea bowl to the ground; the slip of paper splits in two in the wet stain.

zh: 指尖压住纸条一角，不翻也不推，只问他要的这个名字，市价几何。
en: Take the price list with both hands, pile a smile onto your face, your waist already bending three parts down.

zh: 东市茶肆二楼临窗的位置，一个绸缎商把一张纸条推过案面。纸上只写着一个官员的名字，墨迹已干。他将茶碗搁在纸条旁边，碗底在纸上压出一圈湿痕。“上次你在盐商老张那儿‘问’的事，我听说过。”目光越过碗沿，不紧不慢地看着你，“我不是来为难你的。我也是来做生意的。”窗外楼下，东市的骡马队正在卸货，鞭子抽在青石板上的声响传上来。绸缎商从袖口又抽出一张叠好的纸，“这是价钱。你看看。”
en: Press a fingertip onto one corner of the slip—neither flipping it over nor pushing it back—and simply ask what the market price is for this name he wants.

A second-floor seat by the window in an East Market teahouse. A silk merchant slides a slip of paper across the table. Only an official's name is written on it, the ink long dry. He sets his tea bowl beside the slip; the bowl's base presses a ring of moisture into the paper. "That matter you 'inquired' about last time at Old Zhang the salt merchant's—I've heard of it." His gaze passes over the rim of the bowl, unhurried, regarding you. "I'm not here to make trouble. I'm here to do business too." Outside the window below, mule teams at the East Market are unloading cargo, the crack of whips on blue flagstones rising up. The silk merchant draws another folded sheet from his sleeve. "This is the price. Take a look."

zh: 将纸条揉成一团掷还老周，袍子甩回摊上。
en: A Price on the Tea Table

zh: 双手接过纸条，弯腰堆笑：“周爷的事就是我的事。”
en: Crush the slip of paper into a ball and throw it back at Old Zhou; toss the robe back onto the stall.

zh: 捏着纸条不接也不拒，平静开口：“递话可以，但你这摊子得替我瞒三年。”
en: Take the slip with both hands, bend at the waist with a smile: "Master Zhou's business is my business."

zh: 城东的旧衣摊弥漫着霉味和旧尘。你把那件洗得发白的袍子展开——袖口磨出毛边，领子泛黄，正合你经营多年的贫寒模样。摊主老周堆着笑递过来，袖子里却抖出一张纸条。“杜先生，上月南城那封信替你换了五贯，这账我记得。今天这件袍子，就不跟你砍价了——你帮我个忙。”他把纸条往你掌心推了推，上面写着城南韦府一个通房丫头的名字。“你替我给这个人递句话，她的私盐生意我查清了。不递，我就跟左邻右舍讲讲你穿旧袍子替人写密信的事。”
en: Hold the slip—neither accepting nor refusing—and say evenly: "I can pass the message, but this stall of yours keeps my secret for three years."

The used-clothing stall in the east of the city reeks of mildew and old dust. You unfold that washed-out robe—cuffs frayed to threads, collar yellowed, perfectly matching the impoverished appearance you've cultivated for years. The stall owner, Old Zhou, hands it over with a grin, but a slip of paper falls from his sleeve. "Master Du, that letter you wrote for me last month at South City brought in five strings of cash—I remember. Today, for this robe, I won't haggle with you—you do me a favor." He presses the slip into your palm. Written on it is the name of a chamber maid from the Wei residence in the south of the city. "Pass a message to this person for me. I've looked into her private salt business. Refuse, and I'll share with the neighbors the story of how you wear old robes while writing secret letters for people."
The Ledger at the Used-Clothing Stall

zh: 皇城巍峨，朱门深锁。他站在朱雀大街的尽头，远远望着宫墙之内那些飞檐翘角。权谋与荣辱在那里轮番上演，而他只是一个看客。
en: Choose a spot, face north, and settle there.

The Imperial City looms majestic, its vermilion gates locked deep. He stands at the end of Vermilion Sparrow Avenue, gazing from afar at the sweeping eaves and upturned corners within the palace walls. Power and disgrace take turns performing there, and he is but a spectator.

zh: 四方扰扰，竟无一处可安心驻足
en: Gazing at the Imperial City from Afar
The four directions are in turmoil, yet there is not a single place where one may rest the heart in peace.

zh: 平康坊内丝竹声声，歌楼之上有人正唱着一首新词。他在坊间踱步，听着曲声，心底那句「此曲只应天上有」悄悄浮了上来。

en: Within Pingkang Ward, the strings and flutes sound; in the singing halls, someone is performing a new lyric. He paces through the ward, listening to the melody, and from the depths of his heart, that line quietly rises: "This music should only exist in heaven."

zh: 西市喧嚣，胡商牵着骆驼穿过人群，香料、绸缎、宝玉琳琅满目。他在一家胡饼摊前驻足，买了一枚胡饼，边走边看这人间烟火。

en: The West Market bustles; Sogdian merchants lead camels through the crowds. Spices, silks, and precious gems dazzle the eye. He stops before a sesame cake stall, buys one, and walks on, taking in this panorama of common life.

zh: 袖口蹭过坊墙，干土簌簌落下。你继续穿过路口。
en: The Hustle of the West Market

zh: 铁钩刮过石板的声音先于坊丁的身影抵达。你起先以为坊墙下是一堆破被褥，走近三步才看清被褥里伸出的半只手——手指收拢，掌心空着，指甲暗紫色。坊丁走近时你往后退了一步，手不自觉伸进怀里，指腹触到那几枚铜钱，还在。铜钱贴着肋骨，温热。你停了半秒，把铜钱在指间转了一下，按回原处。坊丁弯下腰时你已从他和那具身体旁绕了过去，袖口蹭过坊墙的粗面，带下一撮干土。
en: Your sleeve brushes the ward wall; dry earth crumbles down. You continue through the intersection.

The scrape of an iron hook against flagstones reaches you before the ward guard does. At first you thought the base of the ward wall held a heap of torn bedding. Three steps closer, you made out the half-hand reaching from within—fingers curled inward, palm empty, nails dark purple. When the ward guard drew near, you stepped back, your hand moving unbidden to your chest, fingertip brushing those few copper coins—still there. The coins pressed against your ribs, warm. You paused half a second, turned a coin between your fingers, and pressed it back. By the time the guard bent down, you had already circled past him and that body. Your sleeve caught the rough face of the ward wall, taking a pinch of dry soil with it.

zh: 喉结动一下，袖口拭过案角，往门口走。
信差在门廊外跺着脚上的雪泥。信纸摊在案上，墨迹洇开的地方刚好是“不如早归”四个字。那双冬袜叠得齐整，袜口收针处多绕了两道线——她手冻时才这样收针。你坐下磨墨，笔管在指间转了两圈。纸铺好了。墨磨浓了。手落下去时笔尖停在半空，一滴墨坠在纸上，正好盖住“归”字。你从旧袍腋下拆了一颗木扣子放进信封。信差接过时掂了掂，没说话。
en: Your Adam's apple bobs once. Your sleeve brushes the corner of the desk. You walk toward the door.

The courier stamps snow-mud off his boots outside the doorframe. The letter lies open on the desk; the ink has bled precisely where the words "better to come home soon" are written. The winter socks are folded neatly, the stitching at the cuffs doubled over with two extra passes—the way she sews when her hands are cold. You sit down and grind the ink. The brush handle turns twice between your fingers. The paper is laid. The ink is thick. When your hand descends, the brush tip halts in midair; a drop of ink falls onto the paper, exactly covering the character for "home." You unpick a wooden button from the armpit of your old robe and place it in the envelope. The courier weighs it in his hand as he takes it, and says nothing.

zh: 顿了顿。把下巴搁在最上面那本书的封皮上，朝坊门另一头走。
en: The Letter Home and the Winter Socks

zh: 牛车停在坊门口，车板上的干草簌簌往下掉碎屑。他把书一本一本往你怀里堆，你往后趔趄了小半步——他没看你是否站稳。转身去解缰绳，手指快得像在赶什么东西追上他之前。琴搁在书堆最上面，弦上还绷着昨夜的潮气。你喉咙滚了一下。想说「我也走」——那四个字已经抵在舌根。但你咽回去了。齿关合上时发出一声轻响，像咬碎了一小块脆骨。牛车动了。车轮碾过水沟边沿，琴弦被震出一声闷响——短促，低哑，像被谁从底下踩了一脚。你抱着那摞书站在坊门口。车的影子拉细，缩进春明门方向的灰尘里。
en: Pause. Rest your chin on the cover of the topmost book. Walk toward the other end of the ward gate.

The oxcart stops at the ward gate; bits of dried grass sift down from the cart bed. He stacks books into your arms one by one; you stagger back half a step—he doesn't check whether you've steadied yourself. He turns to untie the reins, fingers moving as fast as if something were chasing him. The qin rests atop the pile of books, its strings still taut with last night's damp. Your throat tightens. You want to say "I'm leaving too"—those four words are already on the tip of your tongue. But you swallow them back. Your teeth close with a soft click, like biting through a small piece of gristle. The oxcart moves. The wheel rolls over the edge of the drainage ditch; the qin string vibrates with a muffled thrum—brief, low, hoarse, as if stomped from below. You stand at the ward gate holding that stack of books. The cart's shadow stretches thin, shrinking into the dust in the direction of Chunming Gate.

zh: 站住。袖口往下坠了一坠。继续往米铺走。
一道老裂痕从云纹中间贯过去，朝奉把它在窗口的光下翻了翻放回柜台。“死当？”你说是。他报的数刚好够付欠了半月的房租和三斗米。你没有还价。帕子在指间叠成方块时，原先包玉的凹处还带着一点余温，四角被玉佩压出的棱硌进掌心。麻绳从栅栏那边推过来，铜钱在绳上沉甸甸地响了一声。你松开帕子，把铜钱拨进袖口——手腕内侧那块被玉焐了十年的皮肉现在贴上了冰凉的方孔。
en: Stop. Your sleeve sinks. Continue toward the rice shop.

An old crack runs straight through the cloud pattern. The pawnbroker turns it over in the light at the window, then sets it back on the counter. "Irredeemable?" You say yes. The figure he names is just enough to cover half a month's overdue rent and three dou of rice. You don't haggle. As the handkerchief folds into a square between your fingers, the hollow where the jade once rested still holds a trace of warmth; the four corners, creased by the jade's weight, press into your palm. The hemp cord with the coins is pushed through from behind the grating; the copper clinks heavily on the cord. You release the handkerchief and scoop the coins into your sleeve—the patch of skin on your inner wrist, warmed by jade for ten years, now presses against cold square holes.

zh: 等了半截入城鼓。你的手从腿边垂下来。
权贵走后半炷香，才有人把酒保往后厨拖。他的靴底在砖缝上划了一下，留下一道深色的痕迹。你看见桌上的碎银子——指甲盖大小，沾着一点血沫。你的手在袖子里张开，拇指碰到两枚铜钱。铜钱是凉的。手慢慢卷回去。旁边有人踢了一脚倒掉的酒坛，酒液还在往砖缝里渗。你站起身，绕过那片湿痕，从另一个方向走了。
en: Wait through half a city-entry drumbeat. Your hand drops from your thigh.

Half an incense stick after the powerful man left, someone finally dragged the wine boy toward the back kitchen. His boot sole scraped across a gap in the bricks, leaving a dark smear. You see the loose silver on the table—fingernail-sized, specked with blood foam. Your hand opens inside your sleeve; your thumb finds two copper coins. The coins are cold. Your hand slowly curls back. Nearby, someone kicks over a fallen wine jar; the wine is still seeping into the brick gaps. You rise, circle around that wet patch, and leave from another direction.

zh: 顿一下。把那截秃笔推还给他。
en: The Wet Stain on the Ground

zh: 他在门口站定时你正数着袖里的铜钱。余光先触到那件青衫——经纬洗得松了，透出里层麻布的纹路。他往前迈了一步，门槛的阴影从他脚背移到脚踝。你听见自己的脊椎一节节凉下去。他问“先生在长安怎么才能被人看见”。你张开嘴。舌根往上颚顶了一下。然后你听见一句话从自己喉咙里出来——“好好写，总会有人看见的”。那声音薄得像坊墙外飘进来的叫卖。他低着头认真点头，袖子里摸出一截秃笔，用唾沫润了润笔尖，抬头说“您再说一遍，我记一记”。你说不用记了。他写字的姿势让你想起十年前租住在城南土墙房里，每天蘸井水在桌上练字的时辰。
en: Pause. Push that stub of a worn brush back toward him.

When he stopped at your doorway, you were counting the coppers in your sleeve. Peripheral vision caught the green robe first—the warp and weft washed loose, revealing the hemp weave beneath. He stepped forward; the threshold's shadow climbed from his instep to his ankle. You felt your spine go cold, vertebra by vertebra. He asked, "Sir, how does one get noticed in Chang'an?" You opened your mouth. Your tongue pressed against the roof of your mouth. Then you heard a sentence come out of your own throat—"Keep writing. Someone will notice eventually." The voice was thin as a street vendor's cry drifting in from beyond the ward wall. He lowered his head and nodded earnestly, fished out a stub of a worn brush from his sleeve, moistened the tip with spit, looked up, and said, "Say it again, please—I'll write it down." You told him there was no need. The way he wrote reminded you of yourself ten years ago, renting an earthen-walled room south of the city, practicing characters on the table with well water each day.
